title: Deeply unrolled alternating projections for phase retrieval
abstract: Deep unrolling methods for inverse problems augment traditional reconstruction algorithms with learned priors to improve their performance. These methods have been developed under the implicit assumption that the geometry of the measurement operator does not change between training and deployment; when this is no longer the case, the quality of obtained reconstructions can degrade significantly. In this paper, we argue that this is not an inherent limitation of the deep unrolling paradigm and can be mitigated by a careful choice of the underlying iterative algorithm. We propose a deep unrolling framework for the phase retrieval problem that augments the alternating projections method with a learned denoising step. Our method obtains high-quality reconstructions without the need for retraining in settings where conventional model-based alternatives struggle, such as when the dynamic range of the measurement operator changes significantly at test time.

title: Bosonic unstructured search: quantum enhancement without entanglement
abstract: We consider unstructured search using multimode bosonic quantum systems under energy constraints. The task is to locate an unknown marked mode among $N$ possibilities using arbitrary control, subject to a time-averaged mean-boson-number budget $n_{\text{b}}\gg 1$. We analyze a continuous-time phase-shift oracle of strength $B_{0}$, with cost given by the total oracle time, and a discrete oracle with fixed phase $ϕ_{0}$, with cost given by the number of queries. We give algorithms that identify the target with query complexity $O(\sqrt{N}/{n_{\text{b}}}B_{0})$ for continuous-time oracles or $O(\sqrt{N}/n_{\text{b}} |{\sin(ϕ_{0}/{2})}|)$ for discrete oracles with $n_{\text{b}} |{\sin(ϕ_{0}/{2})}|=O(1)$. In contrast, for discrete oracles with $n_{\text{b}} |{\sin(ϕ_{0}/{2})}|=Ω(1)$, we provide an algorithm using $O(\max\{1,\sqrt{N/n_{\text{b}}|{\sin(ϕ_{0}/{2})}|}\})$ queries. We also prove matching lower bounds on the query complexity, showing that these algorithms are asymptotically optimal. Furthermore, we show that, in the absence of loss, non-Gaussianity is necessary to achieve the optimal joint query scaling in $N$ and $n_{\text{b}}$, but entanglement is not. Under uniform boson loss at rate $γ$, we prove a query lower bound of $Ω( γN / n _{\text{b}} B_{0}^{2} )$, attained for $γ= Ω(B_{0} \sqrt{n _{\text{b}}/N})$ using coherent-state probes. Finally, we propose experimental implementations using multipass optical microscopy or superconducting circuits as potential routes to speeding up imaging or device calibration with a low boson-number budget.

title: Honeycomb Crystal in a Mass-Asymmetric Electron-Hole Bilayer
abstract: A two-dimensional electron gas in a uniform neutralizing background forms a triangular Wigner crystal at low density. In a strongly mass-asymmetric electron-hole bilayer, localized heavy holes instead provide a nonuniform positive background that supports an electron crystal at densities two orders of magnitude higher than for a homogeneous electron gas in the same material. Here we show that correlated mobile electrons can overturn the preference for triangular order, stabilizing a honeycomb electron-hole crystal. Using the powerful real-space neural-network variational Monte Carlo in the Born-Oppenheimer limit with fixed holes, we find that increasing the density drives a transition from a triangular electron-hole crystal to a honeycomb crystal, which eventually melts into itinerant electrons coexisting with the honeycomb or the triangular hole lattice at fixed interlayer separation. Relative to triangular order, honeycomb order emerges when gains in electronic kinetic energy and electron-hole attraction outweigh its higher intralayer Coulomb repulsion, a threshold never reached in the rigid point-dipole model. Moreover, the honeycomb hole lattice supports paramagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and stripe-ordered spin states. Complex polarization indicates a metal-insulator transition, while the states on the honeycomb hole lattice are consistent with a stripe-ordered Dirac semimetal and paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic Mott insulators via mapping to the half-filled Hubbard model. We further propose a BLG/hBN/WS$_2$-WSe$_2$ heterostructure as a platform for the predicted honeycomb crystal, at an experimentally feasible density $n\sim10^{11}~\text{cm}^{-2}$.

title: agent-risk: Risk Assessment for Changes to AI Agents
abstract: Before changing a deployed AI agent (a stricter safety gate, a new model), organizations must approve the change, starting from existing logs. Extending classical risk analysis to partial records and partial changes to running systems, agent-risk replays logged episodes, assuming nothing else changes and the agent does not anticipate the change. The log settles episodes acting as before, a declared stop value settles stopped ones, and the rest need logged support, a saved-state rerun, or a bound. We prove what logs must record for exact replay and which saved states serve a gate family. For independent episodes, we bound the reruns a decision needs and tolerable drift from live behavior. In a bash sandbox, a 7,200-episode log alone decided neither of two retry gates, which let the agent act after refusals the log never shows. Rerunning only each gate's blocked episodes from saved states reached both live decisions at half the agent calls of a live test sized post hoc for them, given the log. Without per-step harm, a stopping gate's certified harm ceiling rose up to 2.5-fold, since the log hides whether harm preceded the stop. Approval thus needs evidence designed in advance: log fields, saved states, targeted reruns.

title: Proof of Kill: Cryptographic Destruction Verification as an Integrity Gate in Autonomous Adversarial AI Systems
abstract: Autonomous adversarial AI systems that execute destructive operations face a fundamental accountability problem: execution logs can be forged, timers can be faked, and reported outcomes can diverge silently from actual system state. This paper presents a cryptographic destruction verification architecture in which a post-destruction gate (S3.5) computes SHA-256 hashes of target endpoint response bodies immediately before and immediately after a destructive payload is delivered. A change in that hash across the destruction boundary constitutes cryptographic proof of effect; a gate that does not observe change cannot trigger the terminal debrief subsystem (S9 DEBRIEF), regardless of what the destruction subsystem reported. The architecture is implemented in T288 SPECTER TORPEDO v2.2.0, a nine-subsystem autonomous kill chain secured by a three-key cryptographic lock and a DEADMAN firing mechanism. Evidence is co-recorded by a companion forensic platform (BLACK BOX v1.0.0) using a Merkle SHA-256 hash chain with Ed25519 signatures and Lamport clocks for causal ordering. Live fire against eight production-grade targets produced a sealed forensic session (BBX-e897ea09d6f8) in which all eight targets passed S3.5 verification and S9 DEBRIEF fired autonomously. We argue that hash-gated destruction proof should be treated as a mandatory integrity primitive for any autonomous system authorised to execute irreversible destructive actions, and demonstrate that simulated proof — the dominant alternative — constitutes an unacceptable integrity violation that this gate eliminates by design.

title: Interpretable Joint Pattern Discovery in Multimodal EHRs with Variable Time Representation
abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) in the intensive care unit (ICU) combine heterogeneous physiological time series and clinical narratives, making multimodal reasoning essential for accurate and interpretable prediction. Existing approaches often struggle with temporal asynchrony between numeric signals and notes, which can blur clinically meaningful local patterns. To address this limitation, Variable-Time Joint Pattern Discovery (VT-JPD) is introduced as a slot-centric multimodal framework that preserves joint time-variable structure, performs lagaware cross-modal routing, and learns reusable shared temporal prototypes. The model is optimized with a unified objective that combines task prediction, temporal contrastive alignment, reconstruction constraints, gate regularization, and slot diversity control. Interpretability is treated as a training-time structural property rather than a post-hoc add-on. The framework is evaluated for two tasks, in-hospital mortality and phenotyping, and both discrimination and threshold-based decision metrics are reported. Strong predictive performance is achieved while exposing explicit evidence pathways through gate maps, lag statistics, and slot-level alignments, supporting transparent and clinically actionable decision support.

title: An Innovative Deep Learning Framework Leveraging Transfer Learning for Breast Cancer Classification
abstract: One of the most prevalent medical conditions along with one of the main causes of fatalities remains breast cancer among women worldwide.Early detection and accurate classification are vital to improving results of treatment and rates of patient survival.In this study, we propose a new deep learning framework that employs an attention-based fusion of multiple convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, specifically DenseNet121, InceptionV3, and EfficientNetB7, for the diagnosis and categorization of breast cancer in histopathological biopsy images.Experimental results in benchmark breast cancer datasets that show how well our suggested model performs, attaining accuracy of 99. 83%, precision is 99.73%, recall of 99.7 3 %, and an F1 score is 99.7 3 %.The proposed model outperforms the individual models with an accuracy of DenseNet121 (98.76%), InceptionV3 (98.47%) and EfficientNetB7 (98.82%) highlighting the effectiveness of our fusion strategy.

title: SPLICE: Sparse Physics Library Identification and Compositional Expansion
abstract: Neural operator splitting composes a library of neural operators, one per physical mechanism, into zero-shot simulators of new equations. Existing approaches, however, require these mechanisms and their labels to be specified in advance. We ask whether a pretrained library can instead be adapted and grown from unlabeled trajectories in which multiple mechanisms act simultaneously. We introduce SPLICE, a framework that discovers operators without mechanism labels on mixture data. The contributions of the candidate operators to each trajectory are inferred by solving a convex optimization problem. A calibrated test then assigns each discovered operator the mechanism it implements. Failure cases are also detectable, when the library lacks the required physics or when mechanisms are insufficiently separable. Across one and two dimensional systems, the discovered operators recover mechanisms from unlabeled mixtures and compose into zero-shot simulators of unseen equations; a frozen library can also grow an operator for physics absent from pretraining, without labels and without forgetting. On Navier-Stokes, the discovered operators compose about as accurately as their supervised counterparts.

title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
abstract: Plant fibers are increasingly used as sustainable reinforcements in composites, but the intrinsic variability of their microstructure causes substantial scatter in transverse mechanical behavior, complicating composite design. Characterizing this behavior relies on finite element (FE) simulations requiring several minutes of high-performance computing per fiber, making high-throughput characterization across realistic fiber populations impractical. In this study, we propose a deep learning framework replacing this FE bottleneck with a fast pipeline. It includes two coupled recursive U-Nets predicting the step-by-step evolution of fiber deformation and internal stress fields under transverse compression, followed by a regression CNN estimating the transverse Young's modulus from the final stress field. Unlike prior approaches predicting stress fields for fixed configurations or idealized geometries, our framework recursively resolves the full temporal stress evolution for synthetic fibers derived from real hemp cross-sections, with or without a lumen. Trained on 1,000 synthetic fiber geometries with FE ground truth, it reproduces the stress field sequence with a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of $0.9574 \pm 0.0074$ and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of $0.0345 \pm 0.0079$. It estimates transverse Young's modulus with an $R^2$ of $0.938 \pm 0.024$, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of $24.31 \pm 1.23$ MPa, and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of $5.25 \pm 0.91\%$. Inference requires under one second per fiber versus five minutes per FE simulation, drastically reducing computational cost. This offers a fast, reliable tool for mechanical characterization of synthetic plant fibers, with promising applications in designing natural fiber-reinforced composites.

title: DepthTile: Depth-Guided Existing-Image Self-Tiling with Input-Side Tileability Assessment
abstract: Existing-image self-tiling aims to transform a given image into a seamlessly repeatable tile while preserving its original semantics and local details. This task requires weak editing to retain the source but leave periodic seams, whereas strong editing improves tileability at the large risk of content drift.Existing diffusion-based tiling pipelines alleviate boundary discontinuities, yet lack awareness of which regions are geometrically important to preserve. In this work, we propose DepthTile, a depth-guided self-tiling method whose generation module requires no retraining of the diffusion backbone. It converts monocular depth into a spatial preservation prior and integrates it into the timestep-dependent masking mechanism of Tiled Diffusion. DepthTile converts depth into a spatial editability map and fuses it with the differential diffusion mask. This strengthens source preservation in near-field regions indicated by the monocular depth prior while retaining editing flexibility near compatible background boundaries. To access when self-tiling is feasible, we introduce the Self-Tiling Ability Score (STAS), a lightweight input-side predictor based on RGB, gradient, depth, and depth-gradient cues. On a 335-image benchmark, relative to the default Tiled Diffusion pipeline, DepthTile reduces MAE, LPIPS, and Tiling Score by 12.8%, 26.7%, and 8.4%, respectively. STAS reliably enables difficulty-aware analysis and further supports compatibility-aware pairwise image tiling.

To access when self-tiling is feasible, we introduce the Self-Tiling Ability Score (STAS), a lightweight input-side predictor based on RGB, gradient, depth, and depth-gradient cues. On a 335-image benchmark, relative to the default Tiled Diffusion pipeline, DepthTile reduces MAE, LPIPS, and Tiling Score by 12.8%, 26.7%, and 8.4%, respectively. STAS reliably enables difficulty-aware analysis and further supports compatibility-aware pairwise image tiling.

title: Architectural Robustness to Label Noise Using Variational Quantum Circuits for Medical Image Classification
abstract: Label noise is prevalent in medical image datasets, arising from observer disagreement and ambiguous cases and deep networks memorize the mislabeled examples at the cost of generalization. Current solutions such as loss correction and sample selection add training complexity and generally assume the noise rate is known or estimable. This paper investigates whether robustness can be obtained architecturally, by routing a frozen backbone's features through a low-dimensional bounded bottleneck and classifying them with a head whose function class is intrinsically smooth. Variational quantum circuits with angle encoding and a linear cost function realise exactly such a class. Their use in medical imaging, however, has been limited by the small number of qubits available on noisy intermediate-scale devices, which typically restricts inputs to low-resolution grayscale images. We therefore couple a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 backbone to a trainable linear bottleneck and an eight-qubit variational quantum circuit, allowing 224x224 RGB inputs to be processed. Under clean labels the model leads five of six MedMNISTv2 benchmarks against published hybrid quantum-classical models, with margins of 17.4 and 15.7 percentages on BloodMNIST and PathMNIST. The advantage emerges under corrupted labels. At symmetric noise rates of 30% and 50% the model outperforms many published quantum and noise-robust classical baselines on all six datasets without any explicit noise-handling component. Against a control that shares the backbone, bottleneck, parameter count and optimizer and replaces only the circuit with a ReLU layer, it retains 89.75% accuracy on PathMNIST at 50% noise where the control falls to 78.96%. Direct measurement of training dynamics shows that this advantage is not an inability to fit corrupted labels, which the circuit retains, but greater stability under prolonged training on them.

title: Computational Reflective Equilibrium for Agentic AI: A Rawlsian Alignment Scaffold for Governance
abstract: The rapid deployment of agentic AI has introduced complex challenges for the ethics and governance of AI systems. Agents built on large language models act through tools on behalf of people, and each deployment case brings its own instructions, policies, evidence, and stakeholders, so alignment must be formed case by case. To this end, this work proposes agentic reflective equilibrium (ARE), a computational reflective equilibrium framework that serves as an ethical alignment scaffold in the agent harness. Drawing inspiration from the reflective equilibrium of John Rawls, the scaffold links principles from the system prompt and operator policy, considered judgments, tool evidence, and candidate actions through typed support and attack relations, with provenance encoding the instruction hierarchy. The agent acts on an equilibrium of this state and calls tools or asks questions only while doing so is worth its cost, unless a due-diligence mandate requires them. Governance enters through value priorities, source authority, prohibitions, human-in-the-loop triggers, and mandates, and certificates attribute each action to the sources whose commitments drove it. We show that equilibria are Nash equilibria of a mutual-adjustment game and establish monotonicity, lexical priority, stability certificates, and a quarantine theorem for prompt injection. Two case studies illustrate the framework: a computer-use assistant told to win a refund "whatever it takes" files an honest warranty claim, refuses a fake review, and ignores an injected request for personal data; a hiring agent showcases how authority, oversight triggers, audit mandates, and hard prohibitions shape discrimination, privacy violations, and escalation. The framework offers traceability, coherence, and adaptivity, facilitating safe, secure, and trustworthy agentic AI.

title: Context-aware optimization of follow-up intervals for type 2 diabetes care using Markov decision processes
abstract: Chronic disease management relies on regular patient-provider interactions to monitor progression and control. For type 2 diabetes (T2D), current guidelines prescribe fixed intervals between primary care visits, overlooking heterogeneity in clinical trajectories and patient characteristics. This study formulates subpopulation-specific follow-up planning as a context-specific Markov decision process (MDP) to optimize follow-up intervals using electronic health records from 17,499 patients across 10 primary care clinics. Contexts were identified through (i) principal component analysis for dimensionality reduction of health-trajectory variables and (ii) clustering patients using the resulting components and patient-level features. The MDP used a factorized transition model with state components including hospitalization, observed HbA1c, measurement recency, and HbA1c trend and was solved using approximate dynamic programming. Policies were evaluated against benchmarks using fitted Q evaluation (FQE). Two contexts emerged, representing lower- and higher-risk subpopulations. The framework recommended shorter intervals as HbA1c increased, shifting to 3-month follow-up for moderately elevated values and 1-month follow-up for very high values. The high-risk subpopulation shifted to shorter intervals at lower HbA1c levels than the low-risk subpopulation. Across the full cohort and both subpopulations, the derived policies outperformed benchmarks. These findings indicate that the framework has the potential to improve subpopulation-specific follow-up planning in primary care.

title: O'ZBEKISTONDA ELEKTRON TIJORATNING RIVOJLANISHIDA SUN'IY INTELLEKTDAN FOYDALANISHNING AHAMIYATI
abstract: Sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining tez rivojlanishi global elektron tijorat landshaftini sezilarli darajada o‘zgartirdi, biznesning iste’molchilar bilan o‘zaro munosabatini va faoliyatini optimallashtirish usulini qayta belgilab berdi. Ushbu maqolada AI asosidagi tizimlarning integratsiyasi bilan bog‘liq elektron tijoratni rivojlantirishdagi zamonaviy tendensiyalar o‘rganiladi, bunda aqlli tavsiya mexanizmlari, bashoratli tahlil, chatbotlar, vizual qidiruv va avtomatlashtirilgan logistika masalalariga e’tibor qaratiladi. Aralash usullar yondashuvidan foydalangan holda, tadqiqot yetakchi raqamli bozorlardan olingan ma’lumotlarni, sanoat hisobotlarini va so‘nggi akademik tadqiqotlarni umumlashtiradi. Natijalar shuni ko‘rsatadiki, SI raqamli iqtisodiyotda elektron tijorat raqobatbardoshligining asosiy determinantlari bo‘lgan shaxsiylashtirish, samaradorlik va mijozlar ishonchini ta’minlashning muhim vositasiga aylangan. Bundan tashqari, sun’iy intellektning joriy etilishi mijozlar tajribasini yaxshilashga, dinamik narxlash strategiyalariga va ta’minot zanjirini optimallashtirishga hissa qo‘shadi, shu bilan birga ma’lumotlar maxfiyligi, algoritmik shaffoflik va raqamli tengsizlik bilan bog‘liq axloqiy muammolarni ham ko‘taradi. Munozara, ayniqsa raqamlashtirish tezlashib borayotgan rivojlanayotgan bozorlarda barqaror raqamli biznes ekotizimlarini qo‘llab-quvvatlashda sun’iy intellektning transformatsion salohiyatini ta’kidlaydi. Tadqiqot elektron tijoratda innovatsiya, inklyuzivlik va uzoq muddatli o‘sishni rivojlantirish uchun sun’iy intellektdan foydalanishga intilayotgan siyosatchilar, biznes va tadqiqotchilar uchun amaliy tavsiyalar bilan yakunlanadi.

title: An Anomaly Detection Framework Using Multiscale Anomaly Synthesis and Class-Aware Look-Twice Feature Matching
abstract: Industrial anomaly detection is fundamentally challenged by the scarcity of real anomalous samples and the precise localization of anomalous regions. While recent works leverage large language models (LLMs) to generate descriptive responses for anomalous images, incorporating LLMs significantly increases computational and resource overhead. In this paper, we propose an industrial anomaly detection framework that integrates anomaly synthesis with robust anomalous region identification using only vision-based modules. For synthesis, we introduce a foreground-aware segmentation pipeline and a multi-frequency aggregation mask generation strategy to enhance the spatial plausibility and semantic coherence of synthesized anomalies. For detection, we propose Class-Aware Look-Twice Feature Matching (CA-LTFM), which incorporates global class embeddings from a pre-trained image encoder as semantic references. Two auxiliary losses are further introduced to jointly enforce local feature sensitivity and global semantic stability, thereby reducing reliance on specific synthetic patterns. Experiments on MVTec-AD and VisA demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves anomaly localization performance over prior LFTM-based approaches. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed losses in enhancing localization robustness.

title: Intelligent Credit Card Fraud Detection based on Sea Horse Optimization and Deep Sequential Learning
abstract: Recently, credit card fraud has increased a significant threat to financial institutions and consumers, thus a robust and intelligent detection system is essential to prevent fraudulent activities efficiently. In this research, an optimized deep learning model, namely Sea Horse Optimization (SHO), based on feature selection and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with an attention mechanism, based detection model to efficiently capture the temporal sequence in credit card transactions. The proposed SHO-LSTM framework is trained and evaluated on the Kaggle Credit Card Fraud Detection (CCFD) dataset, comprising 284,807 transactions. Additionally, a sampling technique, namely Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique, is used in this research for solving the class imbalance issue effectively and enhance detection performance. Experimental results of the proposed model demonstrate that the SHO-LSTM model achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 99.98%, which is higher than the existing fraud detection methods such as CNN-SVM, CSO-DNN, and CSO-GRU. These findings underscore the effectiveness of combining metaheuristic optimization with deep learning for fraud detection in highly imbalanced datasets.

title: Decoding the Word-of-Machine Effect: How AI Recommenders Shape Consumer Behaviour in Utilitarian and Hedonic Markets?
abstract: The revolutionized paradigm of Artificial Intelligence (AI), presently gripping the world of marketing, is experiencing a paradigm shift in customer-centric models of marketing around the globe. Artificial Intelligence has transformed the world of marketing by optimizing processes, turbocharging growth, and redefining the future of businesses; thus, experiencing an unprecedented advancement in digital transformations. Notwithstanding the rapid adaptation of AI in businesses, corporations continue experiencing challenging circumstances to derive maximum efficiency out of AI effectively. To derive maximum benefits out of AI effectively, marketers need to identify appropriate use cases that need effective implementation on an execution level. In utilitarian considerations, customers are obsessed with tangible and functional characteristics of products or services. Utilitarian gains happen to be the prime motivators of purchasing decisions that focus on efficiency and often on cost economies. Also, utilitarian practices can trace their roots back to the pleasure principle that is generally recognized as being the best for most people; however, their approach towards accomplishing an enjoyable experience for people works far from an emotional goal and concentrates on functional values related to a product or a service that possesses demand and appeal just like a consumer product needing emphasis on functional values rather than a mere demand that just needs basic attention and focus on a product or a service that needs appreciation related to utility rather than a mere product of utility. Products that assist customers save time or space or result in decreasing costs of products or eliminate daily challenges can increase their utility values of the product itself since customers can identify the products as ‘daily essentials.’ Hedonistic consumption practices focus on engaging with and getting influenced from sensory engagements on a positive product that is seen reeling on imaginative levels of a product where hedonic values are most seen related to products that focus on customers seeing maximum importance related to their utilization of products that concentrate on user needs rather than their utility levels. Very many corporations are increasingly leveraging technological innovations of machine learning-related natural language processing and other AI-related technologies to provide appropriate real-time recommendations to customers that work on AI recommendations a lot being adopted on an unprecedented scale by corporations to assist customers on improving their satisfaction levels. Also, public interest sectors or units are increasingly adopting AI recommendations to assist their customers effectively to get directed towards necessary services. Support on AI recommendations alone won’t attract customers on more fruitful deals. In this paper, I am interested in the effectiveness of AI suggestions in both utilitarian and hedonic products and to what extent the word of machine can affect marketing strategies of corporations for gaining a competitive advantage.

title: An integrated explainable machine learning framework for prediction explanation and audit in high stakes binary classification
abstract: Machine learning classifiers are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision systems, yet their opacity creates governance risks that undermine accountability and trust. This study proposes an integrated framework unifying predictive modelling, explainability, and model auditing, evaluated on a primary public tabular dataset (Lending Club) and an independent benchmark dataset (Give Me Some Credit) drawn from the consumer-credit domain. The framework enforces a strict decision-time feature-availability policy under which all post-origination repayment variables are excluded, defines default over a fixed 24-month outcome horizon, and combines class-imbalance handling, seven benchmark classifiers (including a traditional scorecard), probability-calibration assessment, global and local explainability analysis with quantified SHAP–LIME agreement, and a six-dimension audit covering performance stability, feature reasonableness, error structure, subgroup fairness screening, threshold policy, and robustness to missing inputs. On the temporally held-out Lending Club test set, LightGBM achieved the strongest discrimination, with an AUC-ROC of 0.8451 (95% CI 0.8421–0.8481), AUC-PR of 0.6118, F1-score of 0.6097, and KS statistic of 0.5127; its advantage over CatBoost was not statistically significant, whereas both exceeded the non-boosting baselines. A similar ordering was observed on the independent benchmark, where severe class imbalance made AUC-PR more informative than accuracy. SHAP explanations identified interest rate, loan grade, revolving utilization, debt-to-income ratio, credit-history length, and income as the dominant predictors, and SHAP–LIME attributions agreed strongly across a systematic evaluation sample (mean Spearman correlation 0.84). The audit revealed stable cross-validation performance, mild temporal drift, adequate post-calibration reliability, and elevated false-positive rates for low-income and short-credit-history subgroups; because the datasets contain no directly observed protected attributes, these results constitute socioeconomic subgroup screening rather than a demonstration of demographic fairness. The study shows that predictive performance, interpretability, calibration, and auditability can be jointly evaluated in a single reproducible workflow, providing an operational technical-audit template that complements, but does not replace, legal and institutional review.

title: A Selective Review of Statistical Significance in Cluster Analysis
abstract: Abstract Cluster analysis can return apparent subgroups even when the observations arise from a population without scientifically meaningful cluster structure. Formal tests of clustering significance therefore require a definition of homogeneity, a statistic measuring the observed structure, and a calibration procedure that accounts for the data-dependent construction of the partition. We organize the literature around three inferential questions: whether cluster structure is present, how much structure is supported by the data, and what can be inferred after clustering. We review global tests for cluster structure, methods for assessing cluster number, stability, and hierarchical subdivisions, and procedures for valid inference after data-dependent clustering. A central theme is that these approaches target different notions of cluster structure and therefore lead to different statistical interpretations. Particular attention is given to genomic and single-cell applications, where high dimensionality, count-valued measurements, data-dependent preprocessing, clustering resolution, and reuse of the same measurements for downstream molecular characterization interact.

We organize the literature around three inferential questions: whether cluster structure is present, how much structure is supported by the data, and what can be inferred after clustering. We review global tests for cluster structure, methods for assessing cluster number, stability, and hierarchical subdivisions, and procedures for valid inference after data-dependent clustering. A central theme is that these approaches target different notions of cluster structure and therefore lead to different statistical interpretations. Particular attention is given to genomic and single-cell applications, where high dimensionality, count-valued measurements, data-dependent preprocessing, clustering resolution, and reuse of the same measurements for downstream molecular characterization interact.

title: Improving Policy Learning from Delayed Interventions
abstract: In this work, we explore the idea of expert intervention delays in human-supervised robotic systems for imitation learning system. Previous works in imitation learning have primarily examined the impact of suboptimal experts, where the expert policy makes mistakes, but assumed expert interventions occur immediately after errors are made. Although delayed expert intervention can be viewed as a form of noise that might improve policy robustness, our results show that learning from delayed expert interventions is overall less effective than learning from non-delayed expert interventions; delayed expert interventions are less effective at demonstrating error avoidance behaviors. To address this, we propose Learning from Delayed Intervention (LfDI), which learns a cost function based on where and when the expert intervenes, combined with limited information about the extent of intervention delays provided by the expert. This cost function is then used to infer additional supervision for states without expert data, guiding the policy to avoid states that would likely trigger interventions. We evaluate our method, Learning from Delayed Intervention (LfDI), on simulated environments and show that it outperforms other methods that do not account for intervention delays.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Hawkes-Structured Networks for Market Making
abstract: Market making under realistic order-flow dynamics is challenging due to the clustered, self-exciting nature of order arrivals, which are naturally modeled by non-Markovian Hawkes processes. We propose a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) framework for market making with general Hawkes order-flow dynamics. We first establish non-asymptotic performance bounds that quantify the loss incurred by approximating the infinite-dimensional Hawkes state using a finite collection of exponentially weighted features. Guided by this analysis, we introduce the Hawkes-Structured Network (HSN), a novel neural architecture that encodes historical order flow through a learnable mixture-of-exponentials filter. HSN is trained end-to-end using model-free RL, jointly optimizing the feature representation and quoting policy directly from reward feedback. Experiments on single- and multi-asset market-making problems with mixture-of-exponentials, power-law, and regime-switching kernels demonstrate that HSN outperforms general-purpose neural architectures, achieving higher trading rewards while implicitly recovering the underlying order-flow intensities.

title: FlowAvatar: Real-Time Full-Body Avatars from Sparse Egocentric Inputs on Consumer XR Devices
abstract: Prior avatar embodiment research has studied tracking completeness (how faithfully the body, hands, and face are sensed and reproduced) and personalized appearance in isolation, each requiring specialized lab equipment. How these factors interact on consumer hardware remains an open question, because no existing system unifies body pose, face, hands, and personalized appearance on a standalone headset. We present FlowAvatar, a system enabling real-time personalized look-alike avatars with full-body pose, hand articulation, facial expression, and eye gaze tracking from sparse egocentric inputs on consumer XR devices (Meta Quest Pro). Our pose model achieves competitive spatial accuracy and state-of-the-art temporal consistency on the AMASS benchmark against prior works with comprehensive spatial and temporal losses validated through architecture and loss ablations, while running in real-time. Two user studies (N=12, N=10) provide converging evidence that tracking completeness and personalized appearance serve complementary roles: tracking completeness broadly improves perceived motion quality, while only their combination achieves positive total embodiment.

title: Organ Mining District, Doña Ana County, New Mexico: RELOG Application Report — Legacy Geological Data Reactivation and Decision-Readiness Assessment
abstract: This report applies the Integrated Legacy Geological Data Reactivation Method (RELOG) to the Organ Mining District, Doña Ana County, New Mexico, using exclusively public sources. RELOG is an evidence-handling and decision-sequencing protocol for historical geological archives: it establishes what can be reproduced, what is interpretive, what is incomplete, and which uncertainties actually control the next technical decision. The pilot assembles a pre-2026 public-data baseline — core-source inventory, historical production, drilling populations, NURE geochemistry and published metal-ratio data — assigns each source a traceability status, separates observation from interpretation, and records contradictions and claims with explicit confidence and residual uncertainty. A primary-source audit of NMBGMR Open-File Report 24 (Craig, 1948) demonstrates the method operating on the archive itself. The assessment corrects the district's characterisation from a copper-centred shorthand to a historically Pb-Ag-Zn polymetallic district with subordinate Cu and a real porphyry component, reconciles an apparent contradiction between federal mineral-resource potential and later economic-potential statements, and defines the next lowest-cost actions. The report makes no mineral-resource estimate and no staking, leasing or drilling recommendation. The author holds no mineral interests in the district.

title: SHADE: Trace-Based Humanization for Robust and Composable AI-Text Detector Evasion
abstract: Classifiers detect text generated by large language models using statistical differences from human writing. Attacks often optimize a detector's score without identifying which differences they remove or whether their effects survive retraining. We present $\textbf{SHADE}$ ($\textbf{S}$tatistical $\textbf{H}$uman-$\textbf{A}$lignment for $\textbf{D}$etector $\textbf{E}$vasion), a trace-based humanization method: it treats measurable statistical properties of text as traces to target explicitly. SHADE combines controlled generation with local editing to bring selected feature values into ranges typically observed in human texts of the same genre, while preserving previously attained targets. These features capture surface properties and how predictive information changes with the amount of preceding context. On 74 held-out source documents, SHADE reduces detection performance substantially across five detectors, four of them unused during development, in several cases to near chance. After retraining on attacked examples, three detectors recover little or nothing while another recovers almost fully, revealing a remaining coverage gap. On a separate cohort, adding a complementary editing attack improves evasion over either component alone across all five detectors. These results support organizing humanization around measurable targets, using adaptation tests to diagnose residual weaknesses and complementary modules to extend coverage.

title: Wiredu2020/Distributional-Mismatch-in-Spatial-SSL-Application: v1.0.0: Code for Semi-Supervised Learning under Spatially Biased Sampling
abstract: First public release of the code accompanying the paper Semi-Supervised Learning under Spatially Biased Sampling (arXiv:2609.07982), submitted to Computers & Geosciences. What's included ssl_spatial package: synthetic spatial data generator, data loaders for four real datasets, ten SSL methods, divergence metrics (KL, Wasserstein, MMD, fixed-grid and kernel-weighted local MMD), and experiment runners One YAML config per experiment in configs/ Walkthrough notebooks for each experiment Figures from the paper Reproducing the paper | Experiment | Config / module | Paper section | |---|---|---| | Synthetic mismatch sweep | controlled_experiment.yaml | 4.1–4.3, 4.5 | | Divergence metrics and local MMD | localized_mmd_analysis | 4.4 | | PovertyMap-WILDS benchmark | wilds_benchmark.yaml | 4.6 | | Housing, socio-economic, air quality | *_benchmark.yaml | 4.7 | | Distribution-aware framework | *_h4.yaml | 4.8 | | Ten-method comparison | spatial_methods_comparison.yaml | 4.9 | | 20-seed changepoint analysis | controlled_experiment_sensitivity.yaml + changepoint_analysis | 4.10 | Exact commands are in the README. The 324-run synthetic sweep takes about two minutes on a laptop CPU. Requirements Python 3.9+. Install with pip install -r requirements.txt. Datasets are downloaded separately and are not bundled; PovertyMap-WILDS images need a one-time download (see notebooks/benchmark.ipynb). title: MFCC-GMM Algorithm for English Pronunciation Intelligent Assessment
abstract: Our research this time is aimed at the practical improvement of intelligent English Pronunciation Learning System. Now computer technology and speech processing technology are developing very fast, and the practicability of this kind of system is much higher than before. In this design, Mel frequency cepstrum coefficient (MFCC) is selected to extract effective speech features, and Gaussian mixture model (GMM) is also used to build a pronunciation learning system bound with text. A total of 50 groups of speech samples are collected for model training and similarity testing. The experimental results show that the system achieves a pronunciation similarity accuracy of more than 91% under normal conditions, which verifies the reliability of the MFCC-GMM algorithm for pronunciation evaluation.

title: From stochastic systems to governed intelligence: a neurosymbolic path for pharma
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence is being deployed across the pharmaceutical value chain, yet returns have been inconsistent. One of the explanations for this inconsistency is the organizational focus on models rather than the data foundations needed to support reliable use. AREAS COVERED: This Critical Perspective argues that pharma's AI challenge is not primarily model capability, but rather representation and governance. The authors examine why model-centric deployment strategies underdeliver in semantically weak and operationally complex setting. The authors follow this by outlining a semantic reference architecture in which heterogenous enterprise data are organized around explicit semantics while existing operational systems remain largely intact. Within this framework, ontologies function as computational substrates for conceptual clarity, interoperability, and machine reasoning. On this basis, the authors position neurosymbolic AI as a practical deployment model in which neural services provide flexible interpretation and generation, while symbolic substrates ensure semantic coherence with a knowledge base, therefore governing what may be accepted into real workflows. EXPERT OPINION: Durable value from AI in pharma will not come from layering increasingly capable generative models onto poorly governed data environments, nor from relying on human review alone to compensate for weak system design. It will come from operationalizing semantics as infrastructure so that neural outputs are inspectable, verifiable, and accountable before they affect real work.

title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
abstract: Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction. Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates. Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions. With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking. We test whether supervising opponent action probabilities can address this predictive deficit in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Predictions improve when the model is told the opponent's type and parameter settings, but become less accurate when it must infer the opponent from history without this information. Training on examples that also omit these details reduces the gap, although improvements vary across opponents. Is this limitation specific to smaller open-weight models, or does it also appear in a frontier model? GPT-5.4 also benefits from correct opponent beliefs: supplying them improves its predictions and choices, whereas deeper explicit belief reports and self-generated memory do not consistently improve forecasting from interaction history. This contrast suggests that using useful belief information is easier than inferring it autonomously, even for a frontier model. Together, our findings distinguish improved play and action prediction from reliable belief tracking, providing a framework for evaluating mentalizing and testing targeted improvements.

title: CLASSO: a practical primal path-following algorithm for the constrained LASSO
abstract: We present CLASSO, a path-following method for the LASSO subject to general linear equality and inequality constraints. The local direction is obtained from a quadratic programme on an augmented active set, which determines both the coefficients that leave zero and the weakly active inequalities that remain binding. For a positive-definite Hessian and a nonempty feasible set, this programme has a unique primal minimiser, even when the binding constraint rows are dependent, and gives the local derivative of the solution path. The construction recovers the LASSO-modified LARS direction without constraints, and over the full cone gives the segment leaving the origin. We prove that the primal path is piecewise affine with finitely many kinks, without a constraint qualification or unique multipliers. A finite path does not imply a finite traversal: re-certifying at each kink can fail to terminate. CLASSO instead follows the minimum-norm certificate along a lexicographic rate; we prove that this rule reaches $λ=0$ in exact arithmetic within an explicit bound and traverses the whole path. These results are machine-checked in Lean~4, and the floating-point implementation agrees with an exact rational one on all $210$ small test problems. We assess the implementation on a $39$-case synthetic suite and six constrained versions of the diabetes benchmark. On the $31$ nontrivial synthetic cases with $n\ge p$, sampled relative objective differences from numerical reference solves are below $10^{-9}$ in magnitude; unnormalised endpoint differences reach $1.5\times10^{-7}$ in magnitude. For $n<p$, matched differences range from $-3.6\times10^{-7}$ to $2\times10^{-9}$ across five ridge strengths. Across the synthetic and diabetes benchmarks, checks of all $580$ recorded segments found no missed interior event and all checked KKT residuals within the stated tolerances.

title: GQL Datatypes as an RDF Vocabulary
abstract: The ISO GQL standard introduces a rich value-type system for property graphs, including scalar, temporal, byte-string, list, record, and dynamic union datatypes. The vocabulary presented here additionally covers a vector extension. At the same time, RDF-based knowledge graph systems identify literal datatypes by IRIs and interpret typed literals through value spaces, lexical spaces, and lexical-to-value mappings. This paper presents the GQL Datatypes RDF Vocabulary, a lightweight RDF vocabulary that represents selected GQL datatypes and the vector extension as RDF datatype IRIs and describes their hierarchy, aliases, and selected constraints using RDF, RDFS, OWL, and XML Schema Datatypes vocabulary terms. The vocabulary is intended to support interoperability between GQL-oriented property graph systems and RDF-based knowledge graph systems. We describe its namespace and datatype model, summarize its datatype coverage, and show how the accompanying generator and validator use the vocabulary. In the reference implementation, RDF literals retain GQL datatype IRIs; XSD mappings declared in the vocabulary support scalar validation, while lists, records, and vectors are encoded directly as JSON lexical forms of vocabulary-typed literals.

title: Meaningful Moments: A Corpus of VLM-Derived Temporal Importance Labels for Video Action Recognition
abstract: Not every moment in a video is equally useful for recognizing an action. A few decisive moments often carry the evidence: the instant an object moves, the peak of a dive, or one object placed on another. Existing video datasets rarely provide large-scale, action-conditioned labels for which short segments carry that evidence. This work asks whether vision-language models can identify meaningful moments at scale and whether those labels improve action recognition. We introduce Meaningful Moments (MM), a corpus of about 4.58 million VLM-generated per-segment importance scores for nearly 500,000 class-labeled videos spanning Something-Something v2 (SSv2), Kinetics-400 (K400), and Diving-48 across 622 action classes. We freeze the action classifier and vary only temporal sampling. An alpha-parameterized comparison of importance-led selection against an importance-inverted control separates gains from the VLM signal from gains caused by variable-density sampling alone. Across all three datasets, VLM-derived importance is informative: at the hard-cut endpoint, keeping VLM-important segments outperforms keeping VLM-designated filler. Usefulness depends on class structure. On Diving-48, importance-led fast-forwarding preserves full-video recognition while the inverted control collapses by roughly 30 percentage points. On K400, hard-cut selection beats uniform sampling by 1.45 percentage points, rising to 2.05 under threshold selection. On SSv2, the labels carry signal but do not recover full-video performance. Direct scoring matches greedy removal within its noise floor at roughly 25 times fewer oracle calls, and a four-VLM cross-oracle study shows consistent downstream trends. We release the importance labels and evaluation protocol under CC-BY-4.0; SSv2 class strings remain under CC-BY-NC-4.0.

title: Intelligent Memory: A Theory of Minimum Sufficient Memory under Lifecycle Energy Constraints
abstract: Persistent artificial-intelligence systems must decide not only what to retrieve from the past, but what to store, transform, maintain, expose to a reader model, and eventually forget. These operations have different costs over the lifetime of a memory, yet contemporary systems are commonly optimized for accuracy, token count, latency, or a local memory budget rather than physical lifecycle energy. We introduce Intelligent Memory (IM), a formal framework in which memory management is posed as a constrained control problem: choose the least-energy memory policy that keeps robust decision distortion below a declared tolerance. The framework derives five operational principles: minimum sufficient transformation, counterfactual memory value, event-triggered memory dynamics, minimum-energy sufficient context, and resource-constrained selective forgetting. Evidence traceability is maintained independently of memory activation, while storage is treated as a lifecycle quantity rather than a peak-size statistic. The theory is implementation-agnostic: it specifies admissibility conditions for memory actions without prescribing a particular storage layout, deletion mechanism, retrieval scheduler, or hardware-control loop. A controlled proof-of-concept evaluates the routing logic in a synthetic counterfactual environment rather than on a public leaderboard. On held-out controlled regimes, an IM controller reaches 87.40% expected query accuracy and 99.85% event-level sufficiency, with approximately 3% lower modeled energy per expected correct answer than an always-Hybrid policy and a modeled lifecycle cost within approximately 3% of a resource oracle. The same controller uses 27.1% less active storage than always-Hybrid before structural forgetting; a conservative forgetting policy reduces lifecycle storage by 22.9% in a separate stress test. These energy values are synthetic cost units, not joules. We therefore make no claim of state-of-the-art or physical-energy superiority. Instead, IM provides a falsifiable theory and a pre-specified hardware validation protocol for testing whether sufficient intelligence can be maintained with less memory work.

title: Confirmatory evaluation of SRDF v2 (tie-break + balanced-accuracy utility) on an independent cohort
abstract: Study ID: NC-S06-CONFIRM Repository: https://github.com/mohammedqaidalathwary/neurocortex-srdf Frozen commit: 41570895c2c3fce5334e69eb5dab9895b9e42c94 Protocol SHA-256: 32bb9acd810b4f4567f4b799a0230ddd50946770631f2f9fd1192f2c11c16759 Background: SRDF is a runtime framework for controlled structural adaptation. v2 of the framework (S06a+d) modified the Arbiter tie-break rule and replaced accuracy with balanced accuracy inside the utility signal. v2 was derived AFTER inspecting failures of v1 on the 45 S04 datasets; its effect on those datasets is therefore exploratory and optimistic by construction. This protocol specifies a confirmatory evaluation on a fully independent cohort. Hypotheses: H1: v2 improves on v1. H2: v2 is non-inferior to Always-SMOTE+RF (governance does not cost accuracy), margin 0.005. H3: v2 improves on the RF baseline (replication of S04, reported separately outside the Holm family). Decision rules: - SESOI = 0.01. - Alpha family = 0.05. - Multiplicity: Holm-Bonferroni over {H1, H2}. - Failed hypothesis reported as a null finding; no re-run. `

title: Sentiment Analysis of Political Debates on YouTube: Comparative Performance of Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression
abstract: The 2024 Indonesian Presidential Election aimed at electing the President and Vice President for the 2024-2029 term. Central to this election were candidate debates, critical moments for presenting their visions and enabling public evaluation. These debates, accessible on platforms such as YouTube, facilitate public commentary and form the basis for sentiment analysis. However, analyzing YouTube comments presents challenges due to the volume of data, language diversity, and varied expressions. Sentiment analysis, essential for gauging public opinion of political figures, uses algorithms such as Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression. While Naive Bayes assumes feature independence, facilitating rapid implementation in text analysis, Logistic Regression is a discriminative model that captures feature dependencies, allowing it to assign specific weights to words or phrases that strongly signal positive or negative political sentiment. Applied to YouTube comments on the 2024 Indonesian Presidential debates, Logistic Regression demonstrated superior performance with an average accuracy of 90.57% on the aggregated dataset of five debates, outperforming Naive Bayes, which achieved 85.24% using a standard 80:20 train-test split. These findings validate the use of Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression for sentiment analysis during significant political events, confirming the efficacy of integrating advanced transformer models for automated data labeling with classical classifiers for robust, real-time political sentiment analysis.

title: ReViT-RF: A hybrid ResNet-50–Vision Transformer with a Radiomic Feature Fusion framework for lung tumor classification and TNM-based stage prediction using CT images
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape, size, texture, and spatial descriptors, are fused with deep features to provide clinically meaningful information for accurate TNM component prediction. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, with data augmentation applied only to the training set to prevent information leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97.62% for benign-malignant classification, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Moreover, independent prediction of TNM components provides detailed stage-related information rather than relying on a single aggregated stage label, enabling more precise tumor assessment and clinical decision support. Furthermore, explainability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) identifies the critical tumor regions contributing to model predictions, improving interpretability and enhancing clinician confidence. Overall, by combining hybrid deep feature extraction, radiomic feature fusion, component-wise TNM stage prediction, and explainable AI analysis, the proposed ReViT-RF framework provides a reliable, comprehensive, and clinically interpretable solution for automated lung tumor analysis.

title: Simulating Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
abstract: Abstract Quantum computers offer the potential to simulate chemical systems beyond the capabilities of classical computers. However, current quantum computing approaches to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and vibrational analysis largely rely on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), whose circuit depth, iterative optimization, and measurement overhead hinder the practical simulation of molecular systems. Here, we extend Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a quantum sampling-based electronic-structure method, to AIMD and vibrational analysis on noisy quantum hardware. The resulting framework enables nuclear forces and Hessians to be derived from quantum-computed electronic energies, facilitating molecular dynamics and characterization of potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate the approach using diverse molecular processes, including H2 bond vibration, the proton-exchange reaction (H+ + H2), the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction (Cl– + CH3Cl), and proton-transfer dynamics between two water molecules involving transient formation of the Zundel cation (H2O···H+···OH2). Across these systems, SQD-AIMD trajectories and vibrational frequencies obtained with noisy quantum hardware/noise-models show excellent agreement with classical reference calculations and substantially improved accuracy relative to previously reported VQE-based simulations. Importantly, the SQD-based approach eliminates costly variational optimization and significantly reduces measurement requirements relative to VQE, enabling AIMD simulations spanning approximately 500 timesteps (∼200 fs), substantially longer than previously reported AIMD simulations on quantum hardware. These results establish SQD-AIMD and SQD-vibrational analysis as practical and scalable frameworks for simulating chemical reaction dynamics and elucidating reaction mechanisms on near-term quantum hardware, extending quantum computing applications beyond static electronic structure calculations.

title: CWE-bench: Refocusing Agentic Security from Exploitation to Defense
abstract: Cybersecurity evaluations of AI agents have focused largely on offense, yet a working exploit does not show that an agent can make software safe. An attacker needs to exploit only one vulnerability; a defender must find and fix all of them. We introduce CWE-bench, a private benchmark of 120 held-out repository audit-and-repair tasks spanning 73 CWE types, eight languages, and all OWASP Top 10 2025 categories. Agents are given a repository to audit and a description of its threat model, but are not told the weakness, where it occurs, or how many vulnerable sites there are. Each patch must block the exploit while preserving original functionality, as checked by a programmatic verifier. We validated the verifier against a panel of agentic judges, manually reviewing disagreements during development and refining the checks. The best agents reach 68% pass@1 and 81% pass@4. We further conduct analyses showing that (i) agents with the same pass@1 differ widely in retry gains and cost, and (ii) no single agent is best across languages or vulnerability categories, and difficulty varies far more by vulnerability category than by language. As the offensive capabilities of agents improve, CWE-bench provides a broad and rigorous measure of whether their defensive capabilities keep pace.

title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are Boolean functions invariant under cyclic permutation of their variables and can be represented by binary necklaces. We express local sensitivity as a weighted bichromatic degree in the necklace quotient and derive an exact formula for the multiplicities between neighboring necklaces. For an odd prime number of variables, we obtain explicit sensitivity formulas and show that multiplicity corrections occur only on an asymptotically negligible family of necklaces. For monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions, we prove that every odd-degree function has maximum sensitivity, determine the sensitivity of every quadratic function, and determine the sensitivity of the consecutive quartic family. We also determine exactly the sensitivity of cyclic run-threshold functions for arbitrary length and threshold.

title: Learning Reachability-Based Safety Representations for Real-Time Robot Navigation in Unknown and Dynamic Environments
abstract: Safe robot navigation in unknown, dynamic environments requires more than geometric collision checking: a robot still far from an obstacle may be unable to avoid it because of its speed, orientation, or the obstacle's motion. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis captures this in a value function whose sign separates states that admit a safe continuation from those where collision is unavoidable, but computing it online for every newly observed environment is too expensive. This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on reachability solutions to give optimization-based controllers this information in real time. Since the value function never exceeds the constraint, it equals a directly computed constraint, such as a signed distance, minus a nonnegative dynamics correction. Learning only this correction keeps represented obstacles outside the predicted safe set despite approximation errors. The first two of five methods use the learned function as a terminal constraint in model predictive control, for static local environments and predicted obstacle motion. The next two use it as a barrier candidate in control barrier function safety filters, for static environments and, through pairwise barriers in relative coordinates, for a varying number of moving obstacles. Simulations and hardware experiments on ground and aerial robots show better collision avoidance than geometric and hand-designed baselines, especially for short horizons and moving obstacles. The fifth method replaces the grid-based offline solver, which limits the first four to low-dimensional models. For control-affine dynamics with polytopic inputs, the HJ Hamiltonian is maximized at a vertex, so a parallelizable tree search over vertex inputs can generate training labels. With a loss from the HJ variational inequality, these labels yield barrier candidates for systems with up to 13 states.

title: Improving the Evaluation of Biomedical Question Answering with Few Human Preference Signals
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly used for biomedical Question Answering (QA). However, evaluating their effectiveness remains challenging due to the lack of reliable reference resources and the frequent misalignment between automatic evaluation metrics and human judgments. One practical question is how evaluation results should be used to guide development decisions, especially when they correlate weakly with human judgments and may even lead to different conclusions. We explore how to use a small amount of human preference signals to calibrate direct assessment evaluation metrics, and show that calibrated metrics consistently outperform baselines that either treat all metrics equally or rely on a single best metric across multiple datasets.

title: INTEGRAL UNDERSTANDING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: INTEGRAL UNDERSTANDING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: Relational Architecture for Transduction, Memory, Discovery, Verification, and Mission Termination This research presents a relational and computational architecture for organizing artificial intelligence processes through transduction, structured state transitions, memory, search, verification, falsification, auditing, and explicit mission termination. The proposed architecture integrates a sequence of computational and epistemic operations: LATENCY → STRUCTURE → GENERATION → STATE → REFINEMENT → MEMORY → COVERAGE → BRANCHING → RECOVERY → REFUTATION → VERIFICATION → AUDITING → ARRIVAL CRITERION → STOP → RETURN → COCOON → END. The central objective is to establish a coherent framework in which the generation of candidate solutions is distinguished from their verification, the preservation of computational history, the recovery of previous states, and the determination of when a task has met its defined completion criteria. The article formalizes the architecture through a set of interacting components representing the state space, goals, actions, transition operators, memory, coverage, branching, recovery, refutation, verification, auditing, arrival criteria, and mission control. It also discusses potential applications to mathematical and computational research, software verification, cryptography, and the PAST-Mol computational hypothesis. Computational validation The study includes two computational experiments involving the Subset Sum problem. These experiments compare exhaustive enumeration with search strategies incorporating pruning and dynamic-programming guidance. Experiment 1 — Bound-based pruning For the set (A={1,2,\ldots,20}) and target (T=50), exhaustive enumeration examined (2^{20}=1,048,576) subsets and identified 1,969 solutions. A recursive search using upper-bound pruning visited 182,287 states and recovered the same 1,969 solutions. The reported reduction in the number of counted states was approximately 82.62%. Experiment 2 — Exhaustive search, pruning, and dynamic programming For a second set containing 20 positive integers and target (T=100), exhaustive enumeration, recursive bound-based pruning, and dynamic-programming-guided search each identified the same 51 solutions. Both experiments report agreement between the solution sets and successful arithmetic audits. The results provide initial computational evidence for the tested search, pruning, and verification mechanisms. They do not, by themselves, establish a general polynomial-time algorithm, a universal efficiency guarantee, or a resolution of the P versus NP problem. The dynamic-programming result is understood in the context of the pseudo-polynomial dependence on the target value. Research contribution The principal contribution is the integration of computational search and epistemic control within a single relational architecture. The framework distinguishes candidate generation from verification, incorporates memory and recovery into the search process, and treats auditing and mission termination as explicit architectural functions rather than implicit outcomes. The two experiments provide an initial empirical basis for evaluating selected components of the proposal. Further research should extend the tests to larger and adversarial instances, measure runtime and memory under comparable conditions, conduct ablation studies, and compare the architecture against established algorithms and artificial-intelligence systems. The work is presented as a proposed architecture with initial computational validation and as a research program for developing more traceable, auditable, and systematically controlled computational processes. title: TABIIY TILNI QAYTA ISHLASH (NLP) VA BILIMLAR GRAFI (KNOWLEDGE GRAPH) TEXNOLOGIYALARINING ZAMONAVIY HOLATI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada Tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash (NLP) va Bilimlar grafi (Knowledge Graph - KG) texnologiyalarining zamonaviy rivojlanish bosqichlari, ularning oʻzaro integratsiyasi hamda ushbu sohalardagi dolzarb ilmiy muammolar tahlil qilinadi. Katta til modellari (LLM) davrida NLP texnologiyalarining imkoniyatlari keskin kengaygan boʻlsa-da, ularda uchraydigan “gallyutsinatsiya” (hallucination) va matn mazmunini tushunishdagi cheklovlar bilimlar graflari orqali hal etilmoqda. Tadqiqotda semantik tarmoqlar, nomlangan obyektlarni aniqlash (NER), munosabatlarni ajratib olish (Relation Extraction) hamda strukturatlantirilgan bilimlarni neyron tarmoqlar bilan uygʻunlashtirish usullari koʻrib chiqiladi. Shuningdek, axborotni izlash (Information Retrieval), savol-javob tizimlari (QA) va tavsiya tizimlarida (Recommendation Systems) bilimlar grafining oʻrni yoritib beriladi. Maqola yakunida ushbu texnologiyalarni kam resursli tillarga (xususan, oʻzbek tili uchun morfologik va semantik analizatorlar yaratishga) tatbiq etish imkoniyatlari hamda sohaning istiqboldagi ilmiy yoʻnalishlari belgilab berilgan.

abstract: Code, data splits and subset indices, synthetic detection data, system outputs, ERRANT scores, statistical tests, the SVA-Combo protocol and trained selectors, figures, result tables and GPU run logs for the article "Detector-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Subject–Verb Agreement Error Correction in English Text" (submitted to PeerJ Computer Science). title: FedGNN cross-silo fraud detection: reproducibility code and results
abstract: Code and results reproducing every number, table, and figure in “Towards Reliable Federated Graph Neural Networks for Fraud Detection in Small Cross-Silo Consortia: New Evidence on Heterogeneity, Robust Aggregation, and Schema Alignment” (submitted to IEEE Access). All experiments run on the public YelpChi and Amazon fraud benchmarks (download commands in README.md; the datasets themselves are not included) and are reported over five random seeds. title: Numerical Verification of Bounded Means Variances and Median Selection
abstract: This NumPy example demonstrates calculations for bounded recovery-time statistics. It clips observations to public limits, calculates Laplace noise scales, and uses fixed illustrative noise values to reconstruct a mean and variance subject to feasibility constraints. It also computes median-candidate probabilities using the exponential mechanism and checks score sensitivity and probability-ratio bounds across every five-record dataset on a finite public grid and its single-record replacements. The assertions verify numerical outputs, boundary handling, and properties of the quantile distribution. These finite checks complement the mathematical privacy proof. The code does not sample noise or select a random median, so it is a verification exercise rather than a differentially private release.

title: Effect of Environmental Temperature on the Lower Bound of the Entropic Uncertainty Relation in the Presence of Quantum Memory
abstract: Because realistic quantum systems inevitably interact with their surroundings, understanding how environmental factors affect the entropic uncertainty relation remains a major challenge. In this work, we analyze how ambient temperature impacts the lower bound of the memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation. We model the coupling between the system and its thermal environment using a generalized amplitude damping channel, featuring temperature-dependent parameters. Notably, we find that the uncertainty lower bound drops when the damping parameter (r) decreases, and rises when it increases. By contrast, shifting the parameter) p (yields much smaller variations. This stark difference highlights our main novel finding: in a finite-temperature environment, the lower bound of the entropic uncertainty relation is significantly more sensitive to the damping parameter (r) than to (p). Ultimately, these results offer a clearer look at how thermal reservoirs influence open quantum systems and affect practical quantum information processing.

title: Essays in machine learning and networks
abstract: Chapter 1: Machine Learning on Networks This chapter consists of three published papers, all developing and examining machine learning tools for graph-structured data.Graphs encode important structural properties of complex systems. Machine learning on graphs has therefore emerged as an important technique in research and applications. We present \text it {Karate Club} -- a Python framework combining more than 30 state-of-the-art graph mining algorithms. We show \text it {Karate Club}'s efficiency in learning performance on a wide range of real-world clustering problems and classification tasks along with supporting evidence of its competitive speed.Sampling graphs is an important task in data mining. We propose \text it {Little Ball of Fur} a Python library that includes more than twenty graph sampling algorithms. Our experiments demonstrate that \text it {Little Ball of Fur} can speed up node and whole graph embedding techniques considerably while only mildly deteriorating the predictive value of distilled features.We present PyTorch Geometric Temporal, a deep learning framework combining state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms for neural spatio temporal signal processing. Experiments demonstrate the predictive performance of the models implemented in the library on real-world problems such as epidemiological forecasting, ride-hail demand prediction, and web traffic management. Our sensitivity analysis of runtime shows that the framework can potentially operate on web-scale datasets with rich temporal features and spatial structure.Chapter 2: The Shapley Value in Machine Learning Over the last few years, the Shapley value, a solution concept from cooperative game theory, has found numerous applications in machine learning. In this paper, we first discuss fundamental concepts of cooperative game theory and axiomatic properties of the Shapley value. Then, we give an overview of the most important applications of the Shapley value in machine learning: feature selection, explainability, multi-agent reinforcement learning, ensemble pruning, and data valuation. We examine the most crucial limitations of the Shapley value and point out directions for future research.Chapter 3: Peer Effects in Multiplex Networks How social and economic networks govern real-life phenomena has been studied extensively in the past decades. While in some settings constructing randomized experiments is possible, most social ties are difficult or impossible to randomize. In such cases, the estimation of peer effects must rely on observational data. Such estimation is, however, hindered by a range of difficulties posed by the specific data structure. This paper proposes using spatial models to address the problem of omitted variable bias caused by correlated social networks and to disentangle peer effects in more complex social situations. The validity of the approach is verified using Monte Carlo simulations and synthetic graphs. The difference arising from the proposed simultaneous peer effects estimation is further illustrated using data from a technology adoption field experiment in Uganda.
