title: Multiplicative Gradient Method for Log-Homogeneous Optimization: A Unified Mirror-Descent Framework
abstract: Consider the problems of computing $\ell_p$-Lewis weights, Kelly portfolios, D-optimal designs, general equilibria in Fisher markets, and optimal error exponents for channel coding in information theory. All of them can be formulated as optimization problems over the probability simplex, but except for the last one, the associated objective functions are neither Lipschitz continuous nor smooth, rendering existing first-order optimization algorithms and their guarantees not directly applicable. Nevertheless, first-order algorithms for solving these problems do exist in the literature and, perhaps surprisingly, look very similar, even though their interpretations, derivations, and analyses mostly appear unrelated. In this paper, we develop a framework unifying these results that captures their common problem structure through log-homogeneity and a novel second-order condition on the objective function, and identifies their common algorithmic pattern as multiplicative gradient methods. The framework recovers known algorithms and their optimization error guarantees for computing Kelly portfolios, D-optimal designs, optimal error exponents for channel coding in classical communication, $\ell_p$-Lewis weights with $p < 2$, and general equilibria in Fisher markets. To illustrate the insights provided by the framework, we further show that multiplicative gradient methods yield state-of-the-art performance guarantees for computing $\ell_p$-Lewis weights with $p > 2$ and optimal error exponents in classical-quantum communication. Both results are novel to the best of our knowledge.

title: Graph3R: Unifying View Graph Initialization with Feed-Forward Reconstruction
abstract: Feed-forward reconstruction recovers camera poses and dense geometry from image sets whose views are assumed to come from a single scene. In practice, uncurated image collections often contain views from disjoint scenes, and reconstructing these views jointly can corrupt camera poses and geometry. Existing pipelines typically resolve view associations in separate stages before final reconstruction, leaving view graph initialization and reconstruction inference only loosely coupled. We introduce Graph3R, which unifies view graph initialization with feed-forward reconstruction through a shared geometric representation. A lightweight verification head predicts pairwise covisibility from the multi-view features of $π^3$ to construct a view graph. This graph classifies the input views into scene groups. For each group, we mask the shared features before decoding camera poses and dense geometry. Reusing the multi-view features allows Graph3R to reconstruct disjoint scenes separately with a single backbone pass. Across three benchmarks, Graph3R improves average maximum recall at 100% precision by upto 8.99 percentage points over the baseline, while improving reconstruction quality on mixed-scene inputs. Regarding the multi-session mapping task, Graph3R improves cross-session localization and achieves competitive pose estimation accuracy, while delivering a runtime speedup of approximately $35.9\times$ over the baseline when reconstructing the query group. By integrating learned view association with geometric inference, our approach takes a step toward end-to-end reconstruction from uncurated image collections.

title: Research on Anomaly Detection Algorithms Based on Dual-Time-Frequency Pyramids and Consistent Distillation
abstract: To address the challenge of extracting features from multivariate signals under multiple coupling relationships in modern industrial systems, this paper proposes an anomaly detection algorithm based on dual-stream time-frequency pyramids and consistent distillation. This method enhances anomaly detection accuracy and generalization capability by modeling the spatiotemporal dependencies of multivariate signals at the system level. We first designed a multiscale orthogonal decomposition module to separate the original multivariate signal into trend and residual components. These components are then fed into a dual-stream network for time-frequency feature extraction, enabling efficient modeling of diverse system dynamics. Concurrently, a heterogeneous consistency distillation module establishes constraints between the reconstruction and prediction streams, enhancing the detection model’s robust representation of normal operating patterns. This research fills a gap in modeling system-level multivariate coupling relationships and addresses critical limitations of traditional univariate approaches. By employing lightweight modeling and knowledge distillation, it resolves the trade-off between model complexity and industrial deployment. This detection algorithm advances both theoretical understanding and practical scalability in intelligent anomaly detection. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over existing mainstream algorithms across key evaluation metrics for system-level anomaly detection tasks.

title: TradeGraph: Learning Global Semiconductor Market Dynamics from International Trade Networks using Hybrid Graph Neural Networks
abstract: The global semiconductor industry has become a strategic pillar of the digital economy and mainly supports the artificial intelligence technology, cloud computing, advanced manufacturing, and modern electronic devices. Forecasting international semiconductor trade flows is therefore essential for governments, researchers, and policymakers. In this paper, we propose TradeGraph, a hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture that combines Graph Attention Networks (GAT), Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and GraphSAGE through an adaptive gated fusion mechanism for bilateral trade flow prediction. title: Deep learning methods for gamma event selection in TAIGA-IACT image analysis in stereo-mode
abstract: In astrophysical complex TAIGA there are four Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs), located at a distance of 300-500 m from each other, due to which extensive air showers (EAS) generated by cosmic and gamma radiation are recorded by a single telescope or by multiple telescopes simultaneously (stereo-mode). The analysis of EAS images from two or more Cherenkov telescopes together is of particular interest, since for this approach the reconstruction of physical parameters of the primary gamma ray is much more accurate than in mono-observations. However, the gamma-ray event reconstruction strongly depends on the quality of the hadron background suppression of the classifier, therefore, the gamma event selection stage is one of the important ones in the further analysis of IACT data. We propose and study several neural network methods for gamma event selection in joint TAIGA-IACT image analysis. Neural network methods we suggested involves a single-stage analysis of IACT images from two telescopes, while the second method considers the formation of autoencoder-derived essential features that contain the EAS physical parameters, including the type of primary particle.

title: Audit of stale "best known" targets in AI-mathematics benchmarks (data)
abstract: Per-target audit data accompanying the preprint Stale "Best Known" Targets in Benchmarks of AI Mathematical Discovery (Advatiya Thalluri, 2026). Benchmarks of AI mathematical discovery score a model's construction against a stored table of "best known" values. If the table lags the literature, a model that reproduces a published result is scored as a discovery. We checked 268 stored targets from five public sources against the literature: HorizonMath, the Optimization Constants in Mathematics table, EinsteinArena, the AlphaEvolve results notebook, and the AlphaEvolve follow-up paper (arXiv 2511.02864). 69 of the 268 targets (25.7%) are superseded (STALE) or not scoreable as written (MALFORMED). Targets we could not settle (UNCLEAR) are reported separately and are not counted in the 69. Also included: 231 improvement claims by AI-discovery systems with priority verdicts (48 with a prior equal-or-better value, 17 of those from an uncited third party). A verdict of "superseded" requires either a verbatim quote from an opened primary source or a re-score of a public construction using the benchmark's own validator. A blind second searcher re-judged a random sample of 30 targets and agreed on 24 (80%; Cohen's κ = 0.54, moderate agreement on a small sample), with no reversals of a superseded verdict. Version 2 changes:(1) The EinsteinArena re-ranking analysis of version 1 is withdrawn. The platform's authors pointed out that validated submissions on the platform already exceed the literature values used as "audited": on the 2026-10-12 snapshot the top validated submission is better than the best literature value on 8 of 12 problems and equal on 4 (equal at printed precision, or, for the two kissing-number boards, a valid configuration at the literature count). The replacement file gives, per problem, the stated best-known line, the best literature value with source, and the top validated platform score. From this version on, records re-scored with a benchmark's own validator are treated as primary and current.(2) New classical-libraries audit: 158 sampled rows from long-maintained operations-research and packing libraries (TSPLIB, QAPLIB, CVRPLIB, MIPLIB 2017, OR-Library bin packing, circles-in-square, cap-set targets): 0 superseded, 9 not scoreable as written (5.7%). The staleness measured in AI-era tables does not appear in these libraries. Files (README.md first: method, verdict definitions, headline numbers):- cross_benchmark_audit (.csv/.json): all rows for HorizonMath, the Optimization Constants table and EinsteinArena (161 targets)- horizonmath_baselines_audit (.csv/.json) and horizonmath_sources_checked.csv: HorizonMath detail and sources- alphaevolve_notebook_audit and alphaevolve_v2_paper_audit (.csv/.json): the two AlphaEvolve sources- einsteinarena_platform_vs_literature (.csv/.json): stated best-known vs literature vs top validated platform score (new in v2)- or_libraries_audit.csv: classical operations-research and packing libraries (new in v2)- novelty_claims_audit (.csv/.json): priority audit of published improvement claims- second_searcher_agreement.csv: the blind agreement sample Licensed CC BY 4.0. Searches were performed on 2026-10-09, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13 against the pinned versions listed in the README.

title: Causal Ether: From Michelson to the Eligibility Trace -- A Century-Long Search for the Measure of Causality
abstract: In 1887, Michelson and Morley proved the luminiferous ether did not exist. In the decades since, physics has twice re-discovered that causality requires a medium, and twice found that the medium is not a substance but a relation: spacetime geometry for light, curvature for gravity. We present a third instance, this time with systematic experimental evidence. The eligibility trace, e(t+1) = e(t) + w, is a decaying memory that bridges local synaptic events across time to a delayed global reward signal. Five-condition ablation across three scales (N = 800 to 80,000 LIF neurons, up to 128M synapses, 500K training steps, 3 seeds) demonstrates that this equation is the unique necessary temporal structure for emergent differentiation: removing it flatlines the Gini coefficient at random-init levels ( = -0.006 at N=800; flatlines at 0.316 through 500K at N=80,000), while removing any other component preserves or amplifies differentiation. Extending the eligibility window _e from 20 to 200,000 shifts the equilibrium Gini from 0.365 to 0.584 (+60\%, converged, single seed), confirming as the physical parameter controlling asymptotic differentiation. The identical mathematical structure appears in momentum-based stochastic gradient descent and in evolutionary dynamics: three substrates, one equation: differentiation = global signal decaying memory. A causal discovery experiment confirms the time arrow's role: an SNN recovers Granger-causal direction from scalar reward alone, with the eligibility trace amplifying causal signal 17.6 over the no-trace control, while temporal randomization collapses accuracy to near chance. We propose that this structure, the causal ether, is what a century of physicists were reaching for: a medium for causality whose substance is not matter but the arrow of time. The eligibility trace is its first experimentally verified instance.

title: When Fail-Secure Is Not Fail-Safe: Parser Safety in S-100 Maritime Navigation
abstract: Safety-critical maritime navigation depends on machine-readable data products. Their digital signatures establish provenance and integrity but do not guarantee that authenticated content can be parsed safely: even passive data containing no executable code can drive allocation through file-supplied metadata. Using OpenS100, an open S-100 reference implementation, this paper asks whether passive S-102 products can compromise parser memory safety and whether operating system protection alone preserves availability. This paper analyzed the S-102 bathymetric surface specification, built a structurally valid proof-of-concept file with inconsistent grid metadata, and ran it under strong and weak operating system protection across repeated trials. The file triggered an integer overflow and heap buffer overflow without an executable payload. Under strong memory protection, no tested exploit achieved code execution; process termination dominated and the base trigger produced deterministic denial of service, a Fail-Secure outcome that still removed the navigation display. Under weak protection, existing-function reuse achieved Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE) in 14 of 200 launches (7.0%). Neither preserved safe-navigation continuity in the tested application. A four-layer application-level validation sequence applied before allocation prevented both, with no workload-dominant overhead in three desktop microbenchmarks. Passive data are therefore security-relevant parser inputs; preserving both security and availability requires validation before corruption occurs.

title: Exploring University Heritage as Linked Data: A Demonstration of the Jagiellonian University Heritage Metadata Portal
abstract: Historical university heritage resources are often distributed across libraries, archives, and museums, making it difficult to connect information about people, places, works, and events across institutional boundaries. This demo presents the Jagiellonian University Heritage Metadata Portal (JUHMP), developed within the CHExRISH project as a semantic portal integrating metadata from the Jagiellonian Library, the University Archives, and the University Museum into a shared RDF knowledge graph based on CIDOC-CRM. JUHMP supports semantic browsing, entity-centered exploration, curated collections, relationship discovery, recommendations, and SPARQL querying. The demonstration presents two complementary user scenarios: exploratory family-history research through the graphical interface and scholarly biographical analysis using SPARQL. Together, these scenarios illustrate how JUHMP enables users to move from isolated records to interconnected evidence, supporting discovery, contextualization, and reuse of university cultural heritage data. The demo recording is available in the Zenodo repository: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21693797.

title: Beyond Keywords: Training-Free Entity Linking for Research Metadata via Cross-Lingual Retrieval Consensus
abstract: Research databases accumulate rich metadata, including subject keywords, themes, geographic and cultural references, but much of this data remains largely isolated, making it difficult to retrieve and reuse across different databases. The key problem is semantic grounding: without stable identifiers, databases that describe the same cultural practice or geographic region cannot recognise that they do so.

title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and constructions for binary LCD codes
abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$.

title: Critical Components and Market Dynamics of Quantum Sensors: Towards European technology sovereignty in an emerging industry
abstract: Quantum technology is rapidly maturing from academic lab setups to commercially available products and the contours of an emerging global market are starting to become visible. As one of Europe’s leading quantum ecosystems, Quantum Delta NL (QDNL) believes that we have a responsibility to think ahead: what should the future quantum industry look like and how can we anticipate its impact on the economy, society and the global technology landscape? Alongside quantum computing and quantum communication, quantum sensing is an often overlooked area that can be considered, in some respects, the most mature quantum technology. The extreme sensitivity of qubits to their environment, which forms a bottleneck for scaling up quantum computers, is in the case of quantum sensing the main asset that allows for radically new forms of measurements. This can be used for a wide range of applications in many different industries, such as energy, manufacturing, health and defence1. All of these applications require different types of sensors with distinct performance criteria, which can in turn be realised with multiple underlying hardware platforms (i.e. qubit modalities). Moreover, there is no clear, unifying technological goal that everyone in the field is working towards, in contrast to quantum computing and quantum communication networks. This makes it difficult to define a generic quantum sensor and efforts must therefore be focused on specific areas. Within the Dutch ecosystem, three quantum sensing testbeds are being developed as part of QDNL’s Catalyst Programme 3 (CAT-3). The goal of these testbeds is to accelerate the transition from lab to industry for three hardware platforms: cold atoms2, optomechanics3 and nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond4. Achieving this goal requires a clear picture of the critical hardware components required for developing instruments based on these platforms, as well as the strengths and dependencies of the European ecosystem in terms of suppliers. In earlier studies we performed this exercise for quantum computing5 and quantum communication networks6, which resulted in a better understanding of how we can increase our strategic autonomy in this field and the identification of potential actions, such as policy interventions and investment opportunities. These results were also recognised and adoptedIn this study we expand the critical component analysis by including the broader market dynamics in which suppliers and quantum sensor developers operate. By structurally examining the forces at play in this market, we can gain useful insights into how we can support the development of a strong industrial ecosystem in the EU. Combined, this white paper addresses a two-fold central question: what are the critical hardware components of quantum sensing technology under development in the Dutch ecosystem and how is this linked to the broader market dynamics of quantum sensors?

title: Token Exhaustion Attacks (TEA)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) systems bill, throttle and fail in units of tokens. To that end we can then consider the token a security-relevant resource, yet token consumption is still handled mostly as a cost governance problem, through budgets, alerts and per-request caps. This paper proposes the Token Exhaustion Attack (TEA) as a security-first formalisation of deliberate resource exhaustion against LLM-backed systems, whether those systems face customers or are exercised by autonomous agents. It defines the threat, presents a taxonomy of seven attack vectors, and outlines a layered defensive architecture spanning input, output, model routing (AMS) and observability. The central claim is deliberately modest: TEA is not a newly discovered risk, but a risk that warrants the design discipline already applied to denial of service in conventional systems.

The central claim is deliberately modest: TEA is not a newly discovered risk, but a risk that warrants the design discipline already applied to denial of service in conventional systems.

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN ULASAN APLIKASI SIAPKERJA MENGGUNAKAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE DAN RANDOM FOREST
abstract: Abstract: SIAPkerja is a digital employment service platform organized by the Ministry of Manpower of the Republic of Indonesia to facilitate interactions between job seekers and employers. The increasing number of application users has resulted in a higher volume of reviews on the Google Play Store platform, reflecting diverse user experiences and satisfaction levels with the provided services. This study analyzes the sentiment of SIAPkerja user reviews, with 2,000 review data points collected through web scraping from the Google Play Store during the period from October 2022 to June 2026. The data were processed through cleaning, case folding, tokenization, normalization, stopword removal, and stemming, and then represented using TF-IDF weighting. K-Means was applied to cluster public opinions based on analytical patterns and sentiment as the basis for initial label determination, while SVM and Random Forest were used to classify these opinions into positive and negative sentiment categories. SVM achieved an accuracy of 99.63%, which was slightly higher than Random Forest. These results indicate that sentiment analysis based on text mining can be used to evaluate the quality of SIAPkerja services from the perspective of users and can serve as a consideration in formulating digital employment service policies that are more responsive to user needs. Penelitian ini menganalisis sentimen ulasan pengguna SIAPkerja sebanyak 2.000 data ulasan dikumpulkan melalui web scraping dari Google Play Store pada periode Oktober 2022 hingga Juni 2026. title: DIME: Scaling Facial Representation Learning via Differential Masked Autoencoding
abstract: Scaling up data and model capacity has driven substantial progress in visual representation learning. However, conventional pretext tasks exhibit diminishing returns on fine-grained facial analysis. We attribute this to a scaling bottleneck: these tasks model each image's appearance and are dominated by identity, pose, and illumination, so subtle within-identity facial differences contribute little to the training signal. We introduce DIME, a differential masked autoencoder for large-scale facial representation learning. DIME builds on a simple observation: two images of the same person share identity-specific appearance, so their difference exposes facial changes. DIME reconstructs both masked images in an identity-matched pair and, through an Explicit Differential Direction Supervision (EDDS) objective, aligns the direction of their reconstructed difference with the true difference, while source isolation makes each reconstruction depend only on its own image. Shared appearance cancels in this difference, and because EDDS ignores magnitude, subtle facial changes count as much as large pose or illumination changes. DIME uses identity labels only to form pretraining pairs, requires no dense annotations, and learns dense facial representations with emergent part-level semantics. We pretrain DIME on 20 million high-resolution facial images consolidated from existing face datasets. DIME's AU detection performance continues to improve as pretraining data scales from 6M to 20M images, with its BP4D F1 increasing by 5.9 points, while MAE gains only 0.5 points on the same subsets. DIME also outperforms specialized facial methods on AU detection, AU intensity estimation, cross-domain anti-spoofing, landmark localization, head pose estimation, face parsing, and face generation.

title: Boosting the Learning for Ranking Patterns
abstract: Pattern mining is a valuable tool for exploratory data analysis, but identifying relevant patterns for a specific user is challenging. Various interestingness mea- sures have been developed to evaluate patterns, but they may not efficiently estimate user-specific functions. Learning user-specific functions by ranking patterns has been proposed, but this requires significant time and training samples. In this paper, we present a solution that formulates the problem of learning pattern ranking functions as a multicriteria decision making problem. Our approach uses Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to elicit weights for different interestingness measures based on user preference. We also propose an active learning mode with a sensitivity-based heuristic to minimize user ranking queries while still providing high-quality results. Experiments show that our approach significantly reduces running time and returns precise pattern ranking while being robust to user error, compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Spectral Considerations on Unsupervised Time-domain EEG Representation Learning with Deep Networks
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive, scalable source of quantitative biomarkers for the early diagnosis of brain disorders, and deep representation learning has become a powerful paradigm for extracting information-rich latent features from raw signals. However, neural networks tend to under-represent high-frequency information, a concern that is especially acute for EEG given its oscillatory nature and characteristic $1/f^χ$ power decay, which risks masking disease-relevant high-frequency signatures. In this study, we systematically investigate the spectral constraints of unsupervised time-domain feature extraction across three autoencoder architectures (LSTMVAE, VAEEG, Transformer) and a state-of-the-art EEG foundation model. Using synthetic experiments and empirical validation, we show that while autoencoders capture macro-scale shifts such as alpha slowing, they remain biased against higher frequencies due to a magnitude-driven masking effect induced by the Mean Squared Error loss under 1/f-decaying spectra. Increasing latent dimensionality mitigates this attenuation but sacrifices latent compactness and generative stability. We argue that, as the field advances toward large-scale foundation-level feature extractors, it is imperative to move beyond simple time-domain reconstruction and to integrate spectral-domain loss terms and gradient-balancing techniques, so that the subtle high-frequency transients critical for diagnosing complex brain disorders are preserved in the latent representation.

title: The Orchestrator: A Lifecycle Architecture for Self-Developing, Self-Operating, and Self-Improving Agentic Systems
abstract: Agentic systems that perform delegated work also need a controlled way to change the concepts and capabilities on which that work depends. This paper proposes a reference architecture organized around DEVELOP, OPERATE, and IMPROVE, coordinated by a durable orchestration layer. Its central unit of deployment is an immutable operating bundle binding executable capabilities to a versioned semantic snapshot, authority policy, evaluation suite, and state compatibility contract. Operational observations challenge the approved model through discrepancy reports, candidate ontology branches, capability development, independent validation, and explicit promotion. The architecture specifies lifecycle transitions, typed handoff contracts, semantic impact obligations, and deployment fencing. A worked example shows how an ontology change can broaden an action's eligibility without changing policy text, while an independent action gate blocks the prohibited effect. Drawing on autonomic computing, runtime models, ontology evolution, and governed capability deployment, the paper connects semantic release identity to authority review and distributed action enforcement. A conditional invariant argument characterizes release integrity, action coherence, and proposal isolation under stated trust assumptions. The contribution is an architectural synthesis supported by illustrative schemas and a falsifiable evaluation design; operational effectiveness and the additional value of ontology-based controls remain unevaluated.

title: Context-Aware Dictionary Fusion and Lexical Adaptation for Low-Resource Bidirectional Manchu–Chinese Translation
abstract: Manchu–Chinese Dataset Samples: 200 Translation Pairs and 200 Dictionary Entries This release provides two sample datasets for Manchu–Chinese machine translation: Translation samples: 200 Manchu–Chinese parallel pairs selected from the training data. Dictionary samples: 200 distinct Manchu headwords or multiword expressions with their corresponding Chinese definitions. Both datasets are provided in CSV format with three columns: id, manchu, and chinese. Manchu text is represented in Latin transliteration, with redundant whitespace removed. These files are illustrative subsets of the larger resources used in the study, provided to demonstrate their content and structure.

title: COULD WE GIVE A COURSE, OR DO RESEARCH, ABOUT LLMs? Just No — Because the Foundation Is Not Scientific
abstract: Every week, a university announces a new course on Large Language Models. Every week, a research lab publishes a new paper on LLMs. Every week, a student pays tuition, or signs up for free, to learn how LLMs work. The question this paper asks is simple:Should any of this be happening?Not "is it useful." Not "does it work." Those are different questions, with different answers.The question here is narrower, and sharper:Is there a scientific foundation under the thing being taught and studied?If there is, then yes — teach it, research it, build a discipline. If there isn't, then somethingelse is happening, and we should name it. This paper argues: the foundation is not scientific. And it shows what that means, plainly, with sources.

title: "Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes" - Logical Review & Gap Analysis
abstract: Logical Review & Gap Analysis of "Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes" (Minixhofer et al., Nature, 2026; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11111-4), prepared under the Section Zero framework (v2.0). The reviewed paper introduces "byteification": converting existing subword-tokenized large language models into byte-level models using under 1% of a typical pretraining budget (49.1B tokens). It uses a latent-tokenizer architecture with a non-causal boundary predictor and a two-stage procedure (distillation, then end-to-end training). The resulting models (Bolmo 7B/1B, Bwen 8B, Blama 8B) are reported to outperform earlier byte-level models trained from scratch, to reach average scores close to their source models (e.g., 62.5 vs 62.3 for Bolmo 7B vs Olmo 3 7B), to score higher on character-level tasks, and to show higher pass@16 with lower pass@1 on code. This report examines the chain from evidence to claims, based on the paper, its Supplementary Information and the Peer Review File. It identifies five gaps not raised by the authors or referees: (G1) no measures of hallucination, factual fidelity or calibration, which bear on the motivating claim for scientific data; (G2) a comparison with from-scratch byte-level models that does not separate the contribution of the pretrained backbone, and the scope of the "<1%" cost; (G3) no component-level evaluation (encoder, boundary predictor, core, decoder) on the final models; (G4) unmeasured influence of subword-derived design elements and of patches that do not align with subword boundaries; (G5) the direction of the statistical test, the unit of resampling and between-run variance. Each gap is linked to the claims whose reliability it affects. Reliability is assessed per claim. "Conversion is feasible at low training cost, with average scores close to source models" is rated Medium–High. Remaining components are rated Medium, Low–Medium or Low. Claims on scientific data, hallucination and sequence fidelity, multilingual benefits, bias reduction and operating cost are rated "Not yet verified". No claim reaches High. The reliability of the reasoning in this report itself is rated Medium. Keywords byte-level language models; byteification; tokenization; subword tokenization; large language models; hallucination; logical review; gap analysis; philosophy of science; scientific methodology; reliability of claims; evidence assessment; statistical inference; benchmark evaluation; Section Zero

title: Towards Resilience: Slice-Driven Orchestration of Mobile IoMT in 6G-Edge-Continuum
abstract: Emerging healthcare services, such as real-time diagnostics, remote health monitoring and computer-assisted surgery, require stringent Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees while operating under limited and heterogeneous edge resources. Existing Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) orchestration methods primarily focus on communication metrics such as latency and bandwidth, while overlooking edge resource constraints and dynamic adaptation to workload and user mobility. This paper presents a novel resource-slicing-based adaptive orchestration framework that integrates 5G network slicing (NS), resource-aware orchestration, and mobility-aware task offloading into a single adaptive system. IoMT services are assigned to distinct 5G network slices while jointly considering CPU capacity, memory availability and amount of storage, enabling more efficient service placement and execution. In addition, the system supports user mobility and dynamic task offloading to maintain service continuity under changing network conditions. SimPy-based simulation demonstrates that the proposed method enhances service deployment efficiency, reduces request blocking, and improves user acceptance while maintaining reliable performance across diverse IoMT scenarios.

evidence.title: Towards Resilience: Slice-Driven Orchestration of Mobile IoMT in 6G-Edge-Continuum
evidence.abstract: Emerging healthcare services, such as real-time diagnostics, remote health monitoring and computer-assisted surgery, require stringent Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees while operating under limited and heterogeneous edge resources. Existing Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) orchestration methods primarily focus on communication metrics such as latency and bandwidth, while overlooking edge resource constraints and dynamic adaptation to workload and user mobility. This paper presents a novel resource-slicing-based adaptive orchestration framework that integrates 5G network slicing (NS), resource-aware orchestration, and mobility-aware task offloading into a single adaptive system. IoMT services are assigned to distinct 5G network slices while jointly considering CPU capacity, memory availability and amount of storage, enabling more efficient service placement and execution. In addition, the system supports user mobility and dynamic task offloading to maintain service continuity under changing network conditions. SimPy-based simulation demonstrates that the proposed method enhances service deployment efficiency, reduces request blocking, and improves user acceptance while maintaining reliable performance across diverse IoMT scenarios.

title: MAGNET: Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network for Connectome Generation
abstract: Functional brain connectome represents neural connectivity as a matrix of pairwise interactions between brain regions. Generation of functional connectomes is not only a question of validity; rather, having satisfied the constraints on the correlation matrix, the next step is to recover the class-conditional geometry buried under coarse labels. We propose MAGNET, a Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network which uses a normalized-Cholesky representation of the manifold of correlation matrices that guarantees validity. MAGNET lifts noisy latent states into ROI-level region tokens and performs denoising with a relational inductive bias over brain atlas regions. To deal with structural problems induced by coarse labels, MAGNET employs class-anchored conditioning, amortized structural bridge, and relevance-preserving corruption. Across ABIDE, ADNI, and OASIS-3, MAGNET consistently achieves favorable results compared to previous manifold-aware approaches, demonstrating improvements of 7-21% in class-conditional fidelity ($α,β$-F1) across three cohorts and better sampling efficiency. Moreover, while training only with strict binary labels, MAGNET is capable of maintaining clinical heterogeneity through fine substructure of the connectomes in a zero-shot setting, improving subclass covariance alignment ($λ$-MSE) by over 30%. These results suggest that geometric validity is a necessary but insufficient condition for clinical utility in connectome synthesis. Moreover, efforts in making the diffusion denoising class-conditional manifold aware finds utility beyond the highly curved brain connectome generation as this is a critical problem in various general settings. The code repository can be found at https://github.com/protyayofficial/MAGNET.

title: Geospatial Vector Geometry as a Native Spatial Modality for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Geospatial reasoning links VLMs to real-world action and decision making. Reliable reasoning requires accurate spatial information and effective spatial representations. However, current VLMs obtain this information mainly from language and vision. At larger geographic scales, limited visual observations make it difficult to establish accurate spatial references and recover precise spatial relations. This leads to a bottleneck for VLM spatial perception and reasoning. This paper proposes that geospatial vector geometry can become a native spatial modality within a VLM and introduces GeoVec-VLM. First, we develop a structured geometry representation that preserves the spatial structure and arrangement of vector objects, building an explicit spatial basis. Second, we introduce a geometry interaction strategy that brings this basis into multimodal computation, where it interacts with visual content and language references according to the queried spatial relations. Together, these designs allow perception and reasoning to operate on shared geometric references. Across five spatial reasoning tasks, GeoVec-VLM improves mean accuracy by about 11\% relative to the strongest baseline, maintains its gains under geographic transfer, and shows greater geometric consistency. Our results show that geospatial vector geometry offers a promising internal spatial basis for VLM spatial reasoning. https://github.com/TXFR/GeoVector-VLM

title: Locally adaptive step sizes for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods
abstract: Exact reversible locally adaptive step sizes are introduced by Bou-Rabee et al. (2026) in the context of the No-U-Turn Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampler for the purpose of high performance HMC sampling in challenging target distributions. This paper carefully explains and illustrates the locally adaptive step size procedure under more general assumptions. Alternative error measures are introduced with the aim of further enhancing MCMC performance by reducing the prevalence of reversibility failure rejections. In addition, the paper shows how to introduce the locally adaptive step sizes also within standard HMC and Metropolis-corrected kinetic Langevin/generalized HMC (GHMC). Finally, a numerical study of the relative merits of the proposed error measures in the context of different Hamiltonian flow-based MCMC methods is provided.

title: Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach
abstract: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate Rényi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $α$-$z$ relative entropies for $α<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.

title: Hardware-Friendly Token-Group Activation Quantization for Low-Bit Mamba Super-Resolution
abstract: Mamba-based super-resolution models are efficient alternatives to Transformer-based restoration backbones, but their low-bit post-training quantization remains challenging because selective scan, Mamba's input-dependent state-space operator, induces different activation ranges across spatial tokens. Thus, a single layer-wise clipping range poorly matches all tokens. We propose Token-Group Quantization, a hardware-friendly activation PTQ framework that statically approximates a hardware-unfriendly post-scan grouping oracle, where tokens with similar preferred clipping ranges are assigned to the same group. To avoid runtime post-scan grouping in static low-bit inference, a lightweight predictor infers the groups from pre-scan features available before the quantized scan path. During calibration, we form pseudo-labels by clustering post-scan activation descriptors that capture similar rounding--clipping behavior. At inference, the frozen predictor maps pre-scan features to groups and selects entries from offline-calibrated group-wise clipping-bound tables, without runtime statistics collection, dynamic clipping updates, or post-scan group assignment. To address low-bit restoration degradation, we further introduce a Frequency-Preserving Refinement (FPR) objective for clipping-bound calibration. FPR aligns Fourier amplitude and phase between full-precision teacher and quantized student outputs to preserve high-frequency structures. Across PTQ protocols, bit-widths, backbones, and tasks, our method consistently outperforms prior Mamba and SR PTQ baselines, transfers to Transformer SR and Vision Mamba classification, composes with rotation-based quantization, and achieves 2.23x speedup on Jetson Orin Nano over FP16. Code is available here.

title: MAIN DIRECTIONS AND RESULTS OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN THE FIELD OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: This scientific article highlights the main directions of scientific research in the field of artificial intelligence, the results achieved, and their significance in the development of modern society. It analyzes the developmental characteristics of areas such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, and generative artificial intelligence. Opportunities arising from the application of artificial intelligence technologies in the fields of education, medicine, industry, economics, and information technology will also be considered.

title: AMPLIFIED: A Modular Toolchain for Evaluating Deliberative Planning and Verifiable Execution in Robotics
abstract: The wide catalogue of planners enables mission-planning solutions to be tailored to assumptions made on the environment and user needs.However, in robotics, the execution of plans and policies created by these planners is not always straightforward, because autonomous robots deployed in open and dynamic environments undergo fluctuating environmental conditions, partial information, and uncertain execution times. On top of bare engineering issues, planner integration and usability requires reliable and verifiable execution frameworks. We propose AMPLIFIED, a complete toolchain to plan and execute in complex environments, with the goal to assess the quality of the integrated solution. AMPLIFIED is modular, thereby allowing the integration of community-made elements, from the decisional layer to low-level controllers. Building upon an antipoaching scenario, we illustrate how AMPLIFIED can be used to qualitatively evaluate different planners and the executability of their solutions.The complete open-source code is available as a dockerized environment for reproducibility and easy deployment, with results updated as new use-cases, planners and execution frameworks are tested (https://gitlab.com/webots_plugins/amplified_bringup). Finally, a demonstration video showcasing the anti-poaching use-case, both in Webots and in a laboratory setting, is available (https://youtu.be/znwcHL5m1a4?si=vWvNtmclAudmUi2h).

title: Finite-size, quantum-hardware accuracy, and package-shape gates for a sub-kelvin Na2BaCo(PO4)2 magnetic-refrigerator stage
abstract: Reproducible public-data analysis of how finite-size model transfer, weak magnetic interactions, quantum-hardware error, and package demagnetization affect sub-kelvin magnetic-refrigerator decisions for Na2BaCo(PO4)2. The release includes a four-model N=18 transfer gate, a complete nine-circuit IBM Kingston entropy-correction benchmark, engineering decision maps, and package and measurement specifications. The QPU resolves the correction sign but not its quantitative magnitude; no quantum advantage is claimed.

title: Union Interaction Framework
abstract: The Union Interaction Framework (UIF) formalizes a methodological architecture for AI–human co‑construction, defining the union operator 𝑈 = 𝐴 ∪ 𝐻 and the recursive dialogue model through which emergent reasoning arises. UIF provides a reproducible protocol for structured interaction, attractor basin stabilization, and provenance tracking in conceptual co‑construction. It serves as the methodological foundation for the Seven‑Branch Governance (7B) and Enterprise Governance Architecture Program (EGAP) projects, establishing the epistemic basis for union‑constructed governance systems. Provenance: Copilot ∪ JGKees.

title: Visualization and Interpretation of Nuclear Features in a Deep Learning-Discriminant Analysis of Lobular Endocervical Glandular Hyperplasia with VGG16 and Linear Support Vector Machine
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia (LEGH), which is considered a precursor lesion of gastric-type adenocarcinoma, exhibits subtle nuclear atypia in cytological specimens and, thus, is occasionally difficult to distinguish from normal endocervical (EC) cells. In the present study, support vector machine (SVM) and deep learning (DL) using the VGG16 model were applied to investigate whether accurate classification is achievable. METHODS: Papanicolaou-stained microscopic images from 56 EC cases and 47 LEGH cases were used. Several features were extracted from each nucleus, and a classification analysis was performed using SVM and DL. Although cross-validation was performed on a case-by-case basis, accuracy was calculated at the image level because a large number of nuclear images were obtained from each case. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was used to visualize attention regions in DL. RESULTS: For the discrimination between EC and LEGH, the accuracies of SVM and DL were 84.2% and 81.2%, respectively. Accuracies between typical LEGH and atypical LEGH were 64.3% for SVM and 54.0% for DL, showing the largest difference. Grad-CAM visualized the differences in attention regions between EC and LEGH. CONCLUSION: The accuracy of SVM, which uses human-selected features, was slightly higher than that of DL, which automatically extracts and uses features without human intervention. This is presumably a result of humans selecting features that are more effective for discrimination. Grad-CAM showed that, in LEGH, the model evaluated the entire nuclear chromatin and focused on chromatin distribution patterns that are difficult for the human eye to discern.

title: ABSP: Attention-Based Semantic Preservation for Faithful Context Compression
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reduces hallucination in large language models by conditioning generation on retrieved evidence, but retrieved contexts are often compressed before inference to reduce cost and latency. Prior work evaluates compression primarily through answer accuracy, leaving open whether different compression strategies affect how faithfully model outputs are grounded in the provided evidence.

title: Data-efficient pathology whole-slide image segmentation with slide-level conditioning
abstract: Whole-slide images (WSIs) are inherently high-resolution, gigapixel-scale data that require models to reconcile global slide context with fine-grained patch precision, yet progress is often limited by scarce pixel-level annotations. In this work, we address binary foreground segmentation of two histopathological target structures: glomeruli in PAS-stained kidney WSIs and atherosclerotic plaque lesions in murine aortic root sections, where the foreground corresponds to the dataset-specific structure of interest and all remaining tissue and background are treated as non-target regions. We introduce SlideFiLM, a segmentation framework that uses Prov-GigaPath whole-slide representations to guide tile decoding with slide context through a bounded slide-conditioned modulation operator that is shared across tiles. By injecting slide-level context across all tiles, the method achieves end-to-end segmentation on gigapixel WSIs. Across both benchmarks, SlideFiLM outperforms established baselines, with the largest gains for tissue structures that require global tissue context. Crucially, SlideFiLM maintains accuracy in low-data regimes, achieving robust performance under reduced training sets, and shows enhanced slide-level consistency as well as robustness across tissue types. These findings highlight SlideFiLM as an effective solution for WSI segmentation that incorporates global context, providing complete slide coverage, stable performance with limited labels, and consistent gains on structures that depend on broader contextual information.

title: PhysCodeGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Physically Verifiable 4D Reconstruction
abstract: Building physical simulations from video requires coding agents to translate observations into executable models and refine them through tool use. We introduce PhysCodeGym, a benchmark for physically verifiable 4D reconstruction with $156$ tasks covering rigid-body, liquid, deformable, and wind-driven motion. Agents autonomously inspect videos, write and run Blender programs, and revise their scenes using simulation feedback. Six metrics combine rule-based measurements with rubric-based judgments to assess visual and physical reconstruction quality. Program inspection, scene measurements, and counterfactual interventions test physical consistency under original and modified conditions. Experiments with frontier coding agents reveal a tradeoff between artifact quality and completion across reasoning-effort settings, while harness comparisons and agent traces link verification behavior with reconstruction performance. Case studies show that matching visible objects and events can coexist with physical defects. Counterfactual tests further expose latent contact and support failures in reconstructions that pass ordinary physical checks, highlighting the gap between reproducing observations and building reliable physical models. Code is available at https://github.com/ShaoShuai0605/PhysCodeGym.

title: Programmable Floquet Response for Quantum Sensing
abstract: Quantum sensing is typically based on phase accumulation and is therefore fundamentally tied to the coherence time of the sensing system. Here we introduce an alternative sensing paradigm based on programmable Floquet locking in periodically driven two-level systems. We show that periodic control generates an effective Floquet locking field whose orientation and amplitude depend on global offset, allowing information to be encoded in the driven population relaxation dynamics, not in the integrated phase. By controlling transfer between distinct Floquet locking manifolds, external perturbations can be mapped onto engineered relaxation responses whose characteristics are programmable through the driving sequence. We numerically demonstrate this approach for both DC and frequency-selective AC sensing, and show that temporal encoding of the response can provide enhanced precision in the presence of slow instrumental fluctuations. These results illustrate the potential of programmable Floquet responses and open the way to exploring new sensing strategies in driven quantum systems.

title: MaskSense: Confronting the Visual Exploration Trap in Masked Image Generation
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong potential for aligning generative models with human intent, but adapting RL to masked generative models (MGMs) remains largely underexplored. Existing approaches that directly adapt Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to MGMs leave a foundational conflict unaddressed: MGMs' exploitative decoding nature is inherently at odds with the exploratory diversity that GRPO presupposes. In this work, we reveal a structural decoding bias termed the visual exploration trap: confidence-based sampling trades the exploration of diverse subject realizations for the greedy resolution of low-uncertainty background regions, causing premature collapse of the generative exploration space and starving GRPO of the rollout diversity it depends on. To this end, we propose MaskSense, a novel RL framework for MGMs that confronts the visual exploration trap at both the sampling and optimization stages. Specifically, we introduce a semantic anchored routing sampling mechanism that leverages semantic priors to preserve high-entropy subject token exploration while amplifying intra-group reward variance through exploratory-exploitative routing to yield more discriminative advantage estimates. Furthermore, we design a global entropy transition anchoring strategy to identify the most consequential decoding steps and concentrate gradient updates on them. evidence.title: MaskSense: Confronting the Visual Exploration Trap in Masked Image Generation
evidence.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong potential for aligning generative models with human intent, but adapting RL to masked generative models (MGMs) remains largely underexplored. Existing approaches that directly adapt Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to MGMs leave a foundational conflict unaddressed: MGMs' exploitative decoding nature is inherently at odds with the exploratory diversity that GRPO presupposes. In this work, we reveal a structural decoding bias termed the visual exploration trap: confidence-based sampling trades the exploration of diverse subject realizations for the greedy resolution of low-uncertainty background regions, causing premature collapse of the generative exploration space and starving GRPO of the rollout diversity it depends on. To this end, we propose MaskSense, a novel RL framework for MGMs that confronts the visual exploration trap at both the sampling and optimization stages. Specifically, we introduce a semantic anchored routing sampling mechanism that leverages semantic priors to preserve high-entropy subject token exploration while amplifying intra-group reward variance through exploratory-exploitative routing to yield more discriminative advantage estimates. Furthermore, we design a global entropy transition anchoring strategy to identify the most consequential decoding steps and concentrate gradient updates on them. Extensive experiments on multiple text-to-image benchmarks demonstrate that MaskSense substantially improves upon the base model, with GenEval accuracy improving from 54% to 86% and HPS from 28.89 to 36.39, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: pi-Net: Empirical Latent Representations for Differentiable Physics Heads in Data-Scarce Systems
abstract: Developing reliable predictive models for multi-physics systems often forces a compromise between computationally demanding physical simulators and data-hungry, opaque machine learning (ML) algorithms. While incorporating dimensional analysis into directed computation graphs offers a structurally sound alternative to explicitly solving partial differential equations (PDEs), such formulations typically yield underdetermined systems that act as imperfect simulators. We introduce pi-Net, a physics-informed latent variable model that resolves these imperfect simulators. The hybrid pi-Net architecture consists of an encoder that maps inputs into physically normalized latent space, which are then decoded into final predictions by a differentiable physics head. Evaluated on a real-world, data-scarce Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) case study, the framework achieves an R2 of 0.864 with only 60 experimental samples. The results demonstrate that pi-Net significantly outperforms purely data-driven baselines in data-scarce regimes while providing causal, process-level explainability.

title: Topic modeling of the historic file tovima of the University of Patras
abstract: Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εξετάζει την ανεπίβλεπτη ανακάλυψη θεμάτων στο ιστορικό αρχείο της ομάδας ηλεκτρονικού ταχυδρομείου tovima του Πανεπιστημίου Πατρών, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των μηνυμάτων της υποομάδας announcements. Το τελικό σώμα περιλαμβάνει 13.637 μηνύματα στα ελληνικά και τα αγγλικά, για την περίοδο 2018–2023. Η ροή συνδυάζει δομικό και γλωσσικό καθαρισμό, ενσωματώσεις BGE-M3, μείωση διαστάσεων με PCA και UMAP και συσταδοποίηση με HDBSCAN. Οι υπερπαράμετροι επιλέγονται με 200 δοκιμές Optuna. Η εφαρμογή αποτελεί proof of concept θεματικής μοντελοποίησης, με προοπτική αξιοποίησης σε μελλοντική υπηρεσία του Πανεπιστημίου. Η μέθοδος αναδεικνύει 107 συστάδες και 16 κύριες θεματικές, με το 14,7% των μηνυμάτων να παραμένει μη ανατεθειμένο. Η σημασιολογική συνοχή είναι 0,8111, έναντι 0,7999 για το k-means και 0,8005 για τη Ward. Το NPMI είναι αντίστοιχα 0,2067, 0,1892 και 0,1945, με τις πιθανότητες να υπολογίζονται σε κοινό σώμα αναφοράς. Η ανάλυση ευαισθησίας δείχνει μικρή μεταβολή της συνοχής στις τέσσερις διακριτές υπερπαραμέτρους που εξετάστηκαν. Η διαχρονική ανάλυση δείχνει ότι οι συστάδες αποτυπώνουν πραγματικά θεσμικά γεγονότα: η πανδημία εμφανίζεται ως αιχμή του Μαρτίου 2020 σε θεματική που το 2019 σχεδόν δεν υπήρχε, οι πρυτανικές εκλογές κυριαρχούν τον Ιούλιο του 2020, ενώ η εργασιακή θεματολογία αυξάνει το μερίδιό της κατά 3,4 ποσοστιαίες μονάδες μεταξύ 2018 και 2022, χωρίς η συσταδοποίηση να έχει λάβει καμία χρονική πληροφορία.

title: METHODS FOR ENSURING THE INTEGRITY AND AUTHENTICITY OF MILITARY ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
abstract: Background. Orders, intelligence reports and logistics records in military information systems must remain unaltered, be attributable to a known originator, and stay verifiable for years, often over degraded or disconnected networks. Checksums, stored hashes, shared-key message authentication codes and digital signatures are all used for this purpose, but they protect against different threats. Objective. To establish experimentally which threats each mechanism detects, to propose a layered scheme that covers all of them, and to measure its computational cost. Methods. Five schemes (CRC-32, stored SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256 with a group key, Ed25519 signatures, and Ed25519 signatures with a trusted timestamp and a hash-chained ledger) were implemented and tested with 2,000 trials per attack against six attack classes: random modification, modification with tag recomputation, forged authorship by an insider, rollback to an older authentic version, backdating by an author, and deletion. Hashing, signing and ledger verification costs were benchmarked. Results. All schemes detected random modification. CRC-32 and stored SHA-256 detected nothing else; HMAC-SHA256 additionally detected recomputation by an outsider; Ed25519 signatures additionally detected forged authorship; only the layered scheme detected rollback, backdating and deletion (6 of 6 attack classes, with no false alarms on genuine records). Hashing dominated the cost: 130.8 ms for a 50 MB document, while one signature verification took about 0.20 ms. A Merkle inclusion proof for a 262,144-entry ledger verified in about 17 µs, against about 262 ms for a linear chain walk. Conclusions. Integrity alone is not authenticity, and authenticity alone is not freshness or completeness. A signature, a trusted timestamp and an append-only ledger together close the gaps at a modest cost. The attack results follow from the design of each mechanism and confirm the implementation, not field performance; timings are from one machine.

title: PV power forecasting method based on IFCM
abstract: To address the issues of abnormal data interference, insufficient utilization of meteorological similarity, and low temporal resolution in photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional fusion model architecture—the IFCM prediction model—which integrates Isolation Forest (IForest), Fuzzy C-means (FCM), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). This architecture organically integrates three modules—anomaly detection, meteorological classification, and regression prediction—into a complete forecasting framework. Furthermore, to overcome the limitation of the traditional one-hour prediction interval, a refined temporal resolution is designed with a 5-minute sampling interval and a 24-hour forecast horizon (288 sampling points), meeting the stringent requirements of power grid dispatch for high temporal resolution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy under complex weather conditions, such as rainy days, while exhibiting strong robustness and adaptive parameter capability.

title: TriAlign UDA for hybrid domain adaptation of frozen histopathology foundation model representations
abstract: Foundation models produce strong patch-level representations in histopathological image analysis; however, domain shifts across different centers, staining protocols, and scanner conditions can limit the direct generalizability of these representations. In this study, a hybrid feature-level unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework called TriAlign-UDA, which operates on frozen histopathology foundation model representations, is proposed. TriAlign-UDA aims to reduce the mismatch between the labeled source domain and the completely unlabeled target domain without requiring encoder fine-tuning. The method combines statistical alignment, prototype-based semantic preservation, and adversarial adaptation components within a common learning framework based on a bottleneck residual adapter. In the experiments, NCT-CRC-HE-100K was used as the labeled source domain, TCGA-COAD/READ as the unlabeled target domain, and CRC-VAL-HE-7K as the independent external evaluation dataset. In the results obtained over five different seeds, TriAlign-UDA reached the highest mean accuracy of 0.9669 ± 0.0050, balanced accuracy of 0.9560 ± 0.0063, and Macro-F1 of 0.9515 ± 0.0067 on CRC-VAL-HE-7K among the evaluated methods, including the recent EUDA and PLADA-f baselines. DANN and EUDA produced closely competitive results; however, the differences between TriAlign-UDA and DANN, EUDA, or PLADA-f did not reach statistical significance. These findings indicate that frozen-feature UDA should be evaluated not only through individual alignment objectives but also through independent external generalization performance.

title: Matching Randomized First-Order Bounds for Higher-Order Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: Does randomization improve the worst-case first-order complexity of nonconvex optimization when the objective is very smooth? We prove that, for every fixed finite integer $p\ge3$, finding an $\eps$-stationary point requires $Ω_p(\eps^{-5/3})$ exact value-and-gradient queries, even for $C^\infty$ objectives with initial gap at most one and simultaneous global Lipschitz budgets of one for derivatives of orders $1,\ldots,p$. Together with the known deterministic upper bound, this determines the accuracy exponent up to a single logarithmic factor. The lower bound holds for unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, unbounded query locations, and outputs that need not have been queried. One algorithm-independent hard distribution suffices in dimension $O_p(\eps^{-47/3})$. The construction combines a block-chain potential with an exact quartic core, repeated quadratic spectra, and two static Gaussian tensor perturbations. A scheduled Haar argument controls the entire adaptive query span. An innovation-only Gaussian comparison then bounds exact transcript information without assuming finite precision or a minimum query separation. This establishes the $5/3$ randomized accuracy barrier under every prescribed finite smoothness order, extending the previously matched third-order case.

title: Towards Complementary Keypoint Detection via Mixture of Detectors
abstract: Keypoint detection plays a central role in geometric vision pipelines. Existing detectors exhibit complementary strengths across different scene structures and keypoint budgets, and reliance on a single detector often results in suboptimal keypoint distributions. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Mixture of Detectors (MoD)} for dense matching pipelines, a unified framework for complementary keypoint detection through the adaptive composition of heterogeneous detectors. MoD first distills heterogeneous detectors into a unified model, allowing diverse detection maps to be predicted efficiently within a single forward pass. Detector selection is subsequently formulated as a patch-wise, budget-conditioned decision process, in which a lightweight router assigns the most suitable detector to each local region. To avoid heuristic supervision, the router is trained with task-driven rewards derived from downstream matching quality, jointly capturing both keypoint quantity and precision. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, ScanNet, and HPatches demonstrate that MoD consistently outperforms strong baselines across a wide range of keypoint budgets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving keypoint distribution and downstream geometric performance.

title: KARAMEL: Knowledge-Aware Ranking for Multimodal Entity Linking in the Arts via Heterogeneous Graphs
abstract: Discovering and disambiguating entities from multimodal and heterogeneous data is a key challenge in discovery science, where relevant knowledge is often implicit and distributed across modalities. We present KARAMEL, a framework for multimodal entity linking (MEL) - the task of aligning visual and textual mentions to entities in a knowledge base - in the cultural heritage domain. Unlike prior vision-language models that primarily rely on surface-level multimodal alignment, our approach incorporates sociohistorical and contextual knowledge through a knowledge-aware architecture that fuses a vision-language encoder with a heterogeneous graph neural network. This design enables contextual reasoning over complex relational structures and supports robust entity disambiguation under ambiguous or underspecified evidence. To benchmark multimodal discovery in this setting, we introduce WikiMuSA (Wikidata-based Multimodal Semantic data for Art), a new dataset that links artworks to Wikidata entities via images, textual descriptions, and structured contextual knowledge. Experimental results show that KARAMEL surpasses strong baselines, particularly on implicit or abstract mentions, while ablation studies highlight the critical role of domain-specific, structured context in learning expressive representations. While instantiated in the cultural heritage domain, KARAMEL addresses a general knowledge discovery problem and applies to other scientific settings involving multimodal observations and heterogeneous background knowledge. Both the dataset and source code are made publicly available.

title: EgoWholeView: Camera-Only Head-Mounted Capture of Body and Bimanual Hand Motion for Embodied Demonstrations
abstract: Head-mounted body and bimanual motion capture supports self-avatars, teleoperation, and embodied demonstrations. However, a single egocentric camera is vulnerable to a limited field of view, scale ambiguity, and hand-object occlusion. We present EgoWholeView, a wearable capture system of six synchronized wide-angle RGB cameras with a role-specialized pipeline. The outward views localize the rig in a world frame, while an overlapping downward pair independently predicts SMPL-X body and MANO hand parameters. Both predictors are adapted to egocentric fisheye data. To combine the two, reliability cues measured from the predictions themselves weight the fusion of body and hand joint rotations, while shape is aggregated across views and frames. The pair's baseline fixes metric scale, and triangulation recovers root translation. Relative to monocular prediction, fusion reduces PA-MPJPE by 3.7% for the body and 11.2% for the hands, and temporal refinement lowers angular-acceleration magnitude by 32.2% and 31.0%, respectively. On our six-camera recording, the pipeline produces body and hand states in a shared world frame using benchmark-fitted gates without retuning, and temporal refinement lowers hand acceleration magnitude by 41.08%. Using only RGB cameras and no third-person view, EgoWholeView offers a low-cost, portable route to egocentric interaction data.

On our six-camera recording, the pipeline produces body and hand states in a shared world frame using benchmark-fitted gates without retuning, and temporal refinement lowers hand acceleration magnitude by 41.08%. Using only RGB cameras and no third-person view, EgoWholeView offers a low-cost, portable route to egocentric interaction data.

title: Distributed Multi-Agent Learning and Decision Making under Limited Resources
abstract: There have been many developments in the field of robotics in the past 20 years. Some of the more popular advancements involve control systems, multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, and the extension of these systems under limited communication. This dissertation focuses on developing theoretical and practical advancements to multi-agent systems with respect to distributed reinforcement learning, joint action selection, and multi-robot transport problems.However, implementing reinforcement learning in a distributed way is a challenging task which motivates the first part of this dissertation. There are various methods of reinforcement learning that try to solve the issues involving communication and cooperation related to distributed agents; the one we focus on here is Q-learning. Distributed multi-agent communication can be difficult to implement for Q-learning, as all agents must collaboratively choose what actions to take. Thus, we introduce Best Choice Dynamics (BCD), a distributed cooperative joint action selection algorithm that has local optimal convergence guarantees in finite time even under message losses.Q-learning itself typically also struggles to learn the intricacies of a multi-agent system in a distributed manner. Thus we introduce Individual + Cooperative Q-learning (ICQL), a likely counterpart to BCD. ICQL decomposes the Q-values and rewards used by multi-agent Centralized Q-learning to both individual agent and cooperative pair of agents Q-values. This distributed framework allows for extrapolation to partially explored states while the computational complexity scales linearly with an increasing number of agents.The second part of this dissertation is motivated by multi-agent transport problems. More specifically, we introduce a cooperative multi-robots framework that uses robots to carry and transport multiple cargoes via inextensible cables. Each cargo is attached to a pair of robots that can determine the position and height of the cargo based on the robots position. We present high-order control barrier functions (HOCBFs) as a control solution to this robot-cargo framework. We employ an algorithm that checks for feasible/safe configurations of the robot cargo system to ensure that no robot, cargo, or cable collides with each other. We extend the HOCBF controller into a distributed version using Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM).

title: Research on Copyright Identification and Rights Allocation Mechanisms for Generative AI Content: A Case Study of Prompt-Based AIGC
abstract: The current determination of copyright for Prompt-Based AIGC (Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content) based on prompts faces two major challenges: first, the standard for "originality" remains ambiguous; second, the application of neighboring rights is still uncharted. Centered on the core perspective of "educational contribution," this paper proposes a comprehensive framework for assessing originality across three dimensions: the specificity of instructions, the depth of parameter tuning, and the difficulty of result selection. Regarding rights allocation, the paper argues that users should hold copyright, while AI platforms are granted neighboring rights, with developers earning revenue through algorithm licensing. This framework not only helps unify judicial standards but also strikes a balance between technological innovation and intellectual property protection, thereby providing new theoretical foundations for improving China's copyright system.

title: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF ELECTORAL SOVEREIGNTY AND CRYPTOGRAPHIC DEMOCRACY A MATHEMATICALLY PROVEN, QUANTUM-RESISTANT, END-TO-END VERIFIABLE ELECTORAL SYSTEM WITH ZERO-KNOWLEDGE PROOFS AND SECURE MULTI-PARTY COMPUTATION FOR SINGLE TRANSFERABLE VOTE SYSTEMS
abstract: EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF ELECTORAL SOVEREIGNTY: SUMMARY This groundbreaking monograph establishes the first mathematically proven, quantum-resistant, end-to-end verifiable electoral system capable of national-scale deployment, designed as a global gold standard for tamper-proof democratic processes. Six foundational pillars:(1) Zero-Knowledge Proof Authentication using transparent-setup zk-STARKs, eliminating trusted setup controversies while maintaining formal security proofs(2) End-to-End Verifiable Ballots with homomorphic encryption and mix-net protocols ensuring perfect ballot secrecy(3) Quantum-Resistant Distributed Ledger using CRYSTALS post-quantum primitives (Dilithium, Kyber) with Byzantine fault tolerance among 15-21 heterogeneous trustee nodes(4) Secure Multi-Party Computation for Single Transferable Vote with pre-computation phase enabling realistic 12-24 hour result declaration(5) Coercion Resistance combining deniable encryption with innovative Panic Mode UI protecting voters under direct physical duress(6) Risk-Limiting Audits with cryptographic shredding of tracking linkages after 30-day legal challenge period, ensuring permanent ballot secrecy even against quantum computers Four critical innovations addressing real-world vulnerabilities:- Panic Mode UI: Voters enter panic credentials generating convincing fake receipts for coercers while preserving true vote- Pre-Computation Phase: MPC operations completed before election day, reducing WAN execution time to 12-24 hours (3-14x faster than manual counting)- Cryptographic Shredding: Tracking code linkage keys destroyed after legal challenge period, mathematically preventing retroactive secrecy breaches- Transparent zk-STARKs: Default protocol eliminating political vulnerability of trusted setup ceremonies Electoral Robustness Index (ERI) employs Weighted Geometric Mean with Operational Floor quantifying security across cryptographic, verifiability, secrecy, auditability, and quantum resistance dimensions. Economic analysis (Ireland case study):- Capital cost: €32 million- Annual operating: €7 million- Break-even: 5-7 years- Long-term savings: 30-40% reduction in election costs- ERI score: 0.92 (Gold Standard) Comprehensive intellectual property protection covering 6 patent applications under Berne Convention, PCT, and TRIPS. title: Indonesian YouTube Comments on AI-Driven Employment Displacement
abstract: The Indonesian YouTube Comments on AI-Driven Employment Displacement contains a collection of public comments extracted from YouTube comments discussing the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on employment and workforce displacement. The dataset was developed to support research in sentiment analysis, opinion mining, natural language processing (NLP), and social media analytics related to the growing concern of AI replacing human jobs.
