title: MiMaAlign: Hierarchical Micro-Macro Alignment for Physically Plausible Video Generation
abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models have made remarkable progress in generating high-fidelity visuals, yet their outputs still often exhibit physically implausible phenomena, including discontinuous dynamics and implausible event interactions. Existing representation alignment methods mainly transfer generic video features or short-range motion cues, treating physical plausibility as a single-level representation problem. To address this issue, we propose MiMaAlign, a hierarchical micro-macro alignment framework that transfers complementary dynamics-oriented and event-oriented knowledge into different abstraction depths of a pretrained video diffusion model. Specifically, micro-level continuous dynamics alignment imposes constraints by aligning diffusion features with a continuous-time motion representation learned by a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (Neural ODE), while macro-level event-commonsense alignment provides representations of object interactions and event semantics through an instruction-prompted vision-language model (VLM). With training-only auxiliary objectives, we align the complementary supervision from the two teachers with shallower and deeper generator features, respectively, enabling the generator to internalize the corresponding physical priors. Empirical evaluations show that, on CogVideoX-2B, MiMaAlign achieves a relative improvement of up to 21.0% in the Physical Commonsense (PC) score on the VideoPhy benchmark over the baseline, and also delivers substantial gains on the highly challenging VideoPhy2 benchmark, while maintaining general video quality on VBench and being supported by blind user comparisons.

title: Deep Learning and Artificial Intelligence: Conceptual Foundations of Pattern Recognition and Security Applications
abstract: The rapid growth of digital data and the increasing complexity of security threats have expanded the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning in modern security systems. This chapter presents the conceptual foundations of deep learning and pattern recognition and examines their roles in security-oriented applications. It first clarifies the relationships among artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, and pattern recognition, emphasizing the transition from manually engineered features to representation learning through multilayer neural networks. Fundamental mechanisms of deep learning, including artificial neurons, activation functions, forward propagation, backpropagation, loss functions, and hierarchical representation learning, are subsequently discussed. The chapter also reviews major deep learning architectures, including Multilayer Perceptrons, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Autoencoders, and Transformers, with particular attention to their suitability for different data types and security problems. Their applications are examined in the context of intrusion detection, anomaly detection, malware detection, phishing detection, security log analysis, and physical and biometric security. Recent developments involving large language models, federated learning, Edge AI, and continual learning are also considered as emerging directions for security analysis. Beyond predictive performance, the chapter emphasizes that reliable artificial intelligence-based security systems must address several limitations and risks. These include data quality and representativeness, class imbalance, overfitting, data and concept drift, adversarial attacks, data poisoning, model extraction, and membership inference attacks. The discussion further highlights the importance of explainability, privacy, algorithmic fairness, robustness, and human oversight, particularly in high-risk security environments where incorrect decisions may have significant consequences. Overall, the chapter argues that artificial intelligence and security have a bidirectional relationship: artificial intelligence can strengthen threat detection and decision support, while AI systems themselves may become targets of malicious manipulation. Future security systems are therefore expected to rely increasingly on trustworthy, explainable, privacy-aware, adaptive, and human-supervised approaches that combine advanced pattern recognition capabilities with operational and ethical safeguards.

title: Artifact: Strong Control Dependence without Cubic Enumeration
abstract: Anonymous artifact accompanying a paper submission under double-blind review. The paper computes strong control dependence, the decisive-order dependence(DOD) relation in particular, through a compact biclique representation: thesides of each nonempty biclique are extracted in linear time per decision, andclients consume them directly, without enumerating the cubic explicit relation.This yields output-sensitive DOD enumeration and quadratic rooted strongcontrol closure on binary control-flow graphs. Contents- C++ implementation (LLVM 14) of compact inevitability and NTSCD, the biclique DOD construction with its early emptiness checks, rooted dependency closure, and the baselines: Chalupa et al.'s DOD enumeration and NTSCD-and-DOD closure, Danicic et al.'s strong control closure, and a reducibility guard.- A command-line driver that runs one algorithm over every function of an LLVM bitcode file and reports timings and output fingerprints.- Unit tests, including exhaustive differential tests over all 65,536 four-vertex graphs, and a Python reference implementation with a definition-level validator.- The experiment harness and the generator that turns raw results into every macro, table, and figure of the evaluation section.- Inputs: a synthetic family with cubic DOD output, CAV'21-style random graphs, and 133 real-world LLVM bitcode files (GNU Coreutils and open-source applications). SPEC CPU2006 bitcode is not redistributed for licensing reasons; its measurements are included.- The raw measurements behind the paper (per-run CSV, paired summaries, and run configuration). Quick start (needs LLVM 14, CMake, Python 3): build with CMake, run the unittests, then regenerate all evaluation artifacts from the included results with python3 scripts/generate_paper_artifacts.py --closure-baseline cav21 --shared-inevitabilityREADME.md explains how to build the artifact, which results directory backseach result in the paper, and how to rerun every experiment. title: GRAVITY: A Problem-State-Driven Adaptive Computational Intelligence Fabric
abstract: Overview GRAVITY: A Problem-State-Driven Adaptive Computational Intelligence Fabric proposes a constrained framework for allocating computational intelligence, execution strategies, resources, and verification according to the requirements of each problem instance. Modern AI systems frequently frame computation as a model-selection problem: which model should handle a request? GRAVITY extends this framing by considering the broader computational trajectory required to solve a problem, including problem-state construction, context management, capability selection, execution planning, resource allocation, verification, stopping, and escalation. Core Contribution The paper formulates adaptive intelligence allocation as a constrained, multi-objective sequential decision problem. Its central principle, Minimum Sufficient Intelligence (MSI), is to select the least-cost feasible computational strategy expected to satisfy explicit requirements for quality, reliability, risk, and latency. The proposed architecture coordinates heterogeneous computational capabilities, including deterministic algorithms, statistical and machine-learning models, large language models, tools, agents, and human reviewers. It separates hard feasibility and governance constraints from the optimization of competing objectives. The framework provides a common conceptual basis for investigating contextual bandits, adaptive routing, multi-objective optimization, resource-aware scheduling, sequential decision processes, execution orchestration, and outcome verification within a unified computational fabric. Preliminary Evaluation The paper reports a preliminary deterministic Track B benchmark summary using seed 42. In the supplied harness results, GRAVITY reported 100% task success and verification reliability, compared with 50% for the GRAVITY-STATIC control and 100% for the named GPT-OSS-120B comparator. GRAVITY reported 134 tokens per task, compared with 1,270 for the comparator. These figures are descriptive results from the supplied benchmark summary. Task-level logs, sample counts, complete configuration traces, and confidence intervals were not available for independent audit. The results therefore do not establish statistical significance or general superiority across workloads, models, providers, or operating conditions. Research Scope and Future Work The paper identifies a research direction for integrating adaptive computational intelligence into existing enterprise systems without requiring the replacement of their underlying systems of record. Future work includes reproducible multi-workload evaluation, ablation studies, uncertainty-aware decision policies, improved cost and resource accounting, and empirical validation of the proposed architecture. GRAVITY is presented as a research framework and testable architectural proposition. The paper distinguishes its proposed system-level contribution from the established algorithms and methods on which its design draws. Intended Audience This work is intended for researchers and practitioners in adaptive computation, artificial intelligence systems, computational intelligence, model routing, sequential decision-making, multi-objective optimization, resource allocation, AI orchestration, and enterprise AI architecture. Feedback, critical review, and independent reproduction are welcome.

title: Revised Parameterization of Atmospheric Transmittance for Clear-Sky Direct Normal Irradiance
abstract: Despite the significant progress achieved in recent years, there is still room for improving the accuracy of atmospheric transmittance estimation under clear-sky conditions. This study introduces a new parameterization of atmospheric transmittance for estimating direct normal irradiance (DNI). The model equations are derived by integrating the spectral transmittances of the main atmospheric extinction processes into broadband formulations. New empirical corrections are introduced for uniformly mixed gas and water vapor transmittances to reduce systematic deviations from ground measurements. The resulting model, called GM-DNI, was evaluated against high-quality ground measurements collected at eight radiometric stations located on five continents and spanning four climate zones. For the entire test dataset, GM-DNI achieved an nRMSE of 1.84% and an nMBE of 0.22%. The analysis of individual errors showed consistently high accuracy across the investigated conditions, with the best performance at high solar elevations and under low aerosol loading, while no evident dependence on atmospheric water vapor content was observed. Comparison with a reference model places GM-DNI among the most accurate broadband parametric models for clear-sky DNI estimation. The proposed parameterization provides a simple and accurate framework for clear-sky DNI estimation, supporting solar resource assessment and applications requiring reliable direct-normal irradiance data.

title: Epistemic Time: The Clocks of Hypotheses Derived in the Theory of Epistemic Abductive Geometry and Measured in the Epistemic Support-Point Filter
abstract: A possibility field records what evidence has made impossible, and nothing in the field records how it got that way: the same field can be reached by a thousand discriminating observations or declared in one line. The Theory of Epistemic Abductive Geometry (TEAG) closes that gap with a clock carried by each hypothesis, which advances only when evidence changes the field as seen from that hypothesis. This note states the clock from the theory, derives the law that compares the clocks of two hypotheses under the same evidence, and tests the definition and the law on the Epistemic Support-Point Filter (ESPF) on simulated LEO arcs: range and range-rate from two stations and angles only, five and two noise seeds, with and without an undisclosed maneuver, an undisclosed sensor bias, a handover of one filter's posterior to another as a declared prior, and the support threshold varied. The truth is tracked through the filter's fields without ever being used by the filter. The sign lemma of the theory holds in every one of 530,000 cases, and on the real WAAS GEO arc the truth is never demoted at all. The comparison law holds with slope 1.005 to 1.021 and correlation above 0.999 on every run, is exact up to one term that depends on the residual at the prior centre, and is unchanged by the threshold. A filter handed another's field carries the same field, commits to the same states to within centimetres, and has age zero: the clock is the only quantity that separates them. Under a correct model with a sensor finer than the support, the truth accumulates age mainly by surviving the demotion of its rivals; with a sensor coarser than the support, noise-driven demotion dominates every clock, the truth's included, so the signature of truth is the pair of ages together with the impossibility, not the age alone. The age splits into a contraction part and a growth part; on the contraction phase the survived part is a state function and the suffered part carries the order of the evidence, so the ordering dependence of epistemic time lives entirely in demotion. Epistemic time is invariant but not universal: observers in affine coordinates agree what each clock reads, each hypothesis carries its own, and the field decides how fast each one runs.

The age splits into a contraction part and a growth part; on the contraction phase the survived part is a state function and the suffered part carries the order of the evidence, so the ordering dependence of epistemic time lives entirely in demotion. Epistemic time is invariant but not universal: observers in affine coordinates agree what each clock reads, each hypothesis carries its own, and the field decides how fast each one runs.

title: Attention enhanced DeepLabV3+ framework for breast cancer classification
abstract: Timely detection of breast abnormalities with medical imaging is essential for providing more effective treatment, yet remains challenging due to subtle lesion characteristics, low contrast, and complex background structures. Many existing deep learning–based classification approaches rely on whole-image analysis, which may result in missed lesions and more chances of false-negative predictions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes ADSCNet framework, a novel two stage segmentation-guided classification approach designed to enhance diagnostic reliability in breast cancer classification. In stage 1, for precise lesion segmentation DeepLabV3+ with ResNet50 encoder integrated with CBAM into the decoder, where high and low level features are fused is used. Comparative evaluation is performed using several advanced semantic segmentation architectures: U-Net, attention-enhanced U-Net++, and standard DeepLabV3+. The comparison demonstrates that DeepLabV3+ with CBAM outperforms with Mean Dice of 90.14%, Median Dice of 97.19%, and Mean IoU of 86.3% by effectively emphasizing salient lesion regions through its enhanced attention mechanism. The generated segmented masks are then guided to stage 2 for classification where, a lightweight and computationally efficient deep learning model, modified DenseNet121 integrated with CBAM after each of four dense block is employed to classify lesions into cancerous, non-cancerous and normal cases. The segmentation-guided inputs enables the classifier to concentrate on diagnostically meaningful regions, resulting in improved sensitivity and a noticeable reduction in false-negative cases, which is particularly critical in clinical screening applications. In the classification stage model achieves F1-scores of 0.9945, 0.9873, and 0.9947 for normal, benign, and malignant cases respectively, with a good recall for malignant cases. Additionally, an ablation study is also conducted to validate the contribution of changes made in the framework. Further to enhance the generalization capability of proposed ADSCNet framework, cross data validation is performed using UDIAT dataset. Experimental results confirm that the proposed framework achieves improved classification performance. By combining precise lesion segmentation, lightweight classification, and cross data validation, this work demonstrates a segmentation guided approach for breast cancer classification, that may be explored further for successful integration in computer-aided diagnostic systems.

title: A unified differential-equation and operations-research framework for benchmarking metaheuristic optimization of engineering systems
abstract: Tuning an engineering controller or a structural design normally means running a differential-equation model inside an outer search loop: the objective is available only pointwise, carries no usable gradient, and mixes smooth tracking terms with non-smooth actuator saturation and constraint penalties. The search algorithm is therefore itself a design decision, yet it is almost always fixed once, on a single plant, without evidence that the choice transfers to any other. This paper asks whether it does, and when a metaheuristic is needed at all. We answer both questions with a unified differential-equation (DE) and operations-research (OR) framework in which six representative plants—a separately excited DC servomotor, a mass–spring–damper stage, a stirred heat exchanger, a continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR), a series RLC circuit, and an inverted pendulum on a cart—are wrapped in a single proportional–integral–derivative (PID) evaluation harness, alongside three constrained mechanical-design benchmarks and the ten-dimensional Rastrigin function. Seven long-established metaheuristics (GA, PSO, DE, SA, GWO, WOA, SCA) are compared over fifteen seeded runs at a budget of exactly 3000 objective evaluations, enforced by an evaluation counter rather than by nominal population and iteration settings, so that trajectory- and population-based solvers are treated identically. Four non-metaheuristic baselines, a hyperparameter sensitivity sweep and two ablation studies test the framework itself. The solver ranking reverses across problem classes: differential evolution attains the best Friedman rank on the PID landscapes (1.52 of 7) where the sine–cosine algorithm is worst (6.44), whereas on Rastrigin that ordering inverts (SCA 1.20, WOA 2.07, DE 5.60), and GWO and DE dominate the constrained designs. The baselines explain why. On the smooth PID surfaces a multi-start Nelder–Mead search matches every metaheuristic to five decimal places, so the metaheuristic buys robustness rather than accuracy; classical Ziegler–Nichols tuning, by contrast, is 8.9 to 19.8 times worse, and no local method remains competitive once constraints or multimodality are present. The framework therefore does more than rank solvers—it identifies which problems justify a metaheuristic—and is released as a fully specified, reproducible pipeline.

title: Generative Models as Adaptive Trust Regions for Discrete Bayesian Optimisation
abstract: Bayesian optimisation (BO) is a powerful framework for sample-efficient optimisation of expensive black-box functions, but its application to high-dimensional discrete scientific design remains challenging. Local trust-region BO methods such as TuRBO address high dimensionality by restricting search to adaptively sized neighbourhoods. However, a direct discrete analogue based on edit distance can be poorly suited to structured discrete objects: neighbourhoods grow combinatorially, and metric proximity does not capture the dependencies that determine whether a design is plausible or useful. Motivated by the growing availability of pretrained generative models, we introduce GenTuRBO, which replaces the geometric trust region with an adaptively scaled proposal distribution defined by a pretrained generator. The generator provides a learned prior over discrete transformations, encoding coordinated changes without explicitly enumerating edit-distance neighbourhoods. GenTuRBO performs strongly across all three domains and achieves the highest mean final scores on Ehrlich sequence optimisation and Sokoban coordination.

title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

title: PXRD-Bench: How Close Are We to Determining Crystal Structures from Powder Diffraction?
abstract: Determining crystal structures from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) would enable routine characterization of newly synthesized materials, including those absent from reference databases. Generative models offer a promising approach, but existing evaluations remain fragmented and largely assume single-phase samples with known composition. To fill this gap, we introduce PXRD-Bench, a unified benchmark that extends evaluation to unknown per-element atom counts and recovery of both structures in two-phase mixtures. It provides approximately 4.1 million training structures with simulated PXRD, tests generalization to unseen compositions and structural prototypes, and evaluates recovery from experimental PXRD after excluding structurally matching training entries. To provide a strong reference baseline, we also introduce Bragglite, a PXRD-to-structure model developed through a systematic study of PXRD modeling choices. It achieves a 44.2\% Top-1 match rate on experimental RRUFF patterns with known composition, 24.6\% above the strongest prior baseline. Further analysis yields several key findings: some models fail to benefit from experimental PXRD, while generalization to unseen structural prototypes and recovery from two-phase mixtures remain challenging. Together, our benchmark, systematic studies, and Bragglite clarify the capabilities and limitations of current PXRD-to-structure models.

title: NetRL: Powering Network Decisions via NetGRPO-Driven Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Network decision-making tasks, including adaptive bitrate streaming, load balancing, and congestion control, require policies to process heterogeneous states and actions while balancing near- and long-term consequences. Existing solutions generalize poorly across network tasks, require substantial task-specific redesign, and lack reliable evaluation of long- horizon action consequences. Methods that learn through online interaction additionally face unstable optimization. We present NetRL, a two-stage LLM-based reinforcement learning framework that combines supervised fine-tuning on demonstration trajectories with online policy optimization. A universal mixed-embedding interface combines textual task descriptions with precise numerical states, while a network action head produces valid decisions. At its core, NetGRPO evaluates candidate actions over multiple future trajectories, directs deeper search toward uncertain alternatives through confidence-aware budgeting, and performs group-relative, clipped, and KL-regularized updates. NetRL achieves 23.6% higher QoE than NetLLM, 12.2% lower job completion time than Genet, and 24.1% higher network utility than Orca, yielding state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods. Confidence-aware budgeting reduces end-to-end training time by 27.1% without reducing validation QoE. NetRL also converges stably and generalizes to unseen network traces without retraining. Code and model weights are available at the repository linked in this paper.

title: Design and development of adaptive educational software that dynamically adjusts to user input
abstract: Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία έχει ως αντικείμενο τον σχεδιασμό και την ανάπτυξη του PySkills Tutor, μιας πρωτότυπης διαδικτυακής πλατφόρμας προσαρμοστικής εκμάθησης της γλώσσας προγραμματισμού Python. Η εργασία εστιάζει στην ανάγκη υποστήριξης αρχάριων μαθητών, οι οποίοι συχνά ξεκινούν από διαφορετικό επίπεδο γνώσεων και αντιμετωπίζουν διαφορετικές δυσκολίες κατά την εκμάθηση βασικών εννοιών προγραμματισμού. Στο πλαίσιο της εργασίας αναπτύχθηκε ένα σύστημα που οργανώνει το εκπαιδευτικό περιεχόμενο σε μαθήματα, επίπεδα, δεξιότητες και δραστηριότητες. Η πλατφόρμα υποστηρίζει διακριτούς ρόλους μαθητή και εκπαιδευτικού, αρχική αξιολόγηση μέσω pre-test, παρακολούθηση προόδου ανά δεξιότητα, μηχανισμό επιλογής επόμενης δραστηριότητας και δυνατότητα τελικής αξιολόγησης μέσω post-test. Ο προσαρμοστικός μηχανισμός βασίζεται σε δεδομένα επίδοσης και αλληλεπίδρασης του μαθητή, όπως οι προσπάθειες, η ακρίβεια, τα συνεχόμενα λάθη και η κατάσταση mastery. Η υλοποίηση του PySkills Tutor βασίστηκε σε σύγχρονες τεχνολογίες διαδικτυακών εφαρμογών, με backend σε FastAPI, σχεσιακή βάση δεδομένων PostgreSQL και frontend με HTML templates. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δόθηκε στην οργάνωση της αρχιτεκτονικής, στη διαχείριση των βασικών οντοτήτων του συστήματος, στην αυθεντικοποίηση χρηστών, στη διάκριση δικαιωμάτων πρόσβασης και στη λειτουργική επαλήθευση των βασικών ροών της πλατφόρμας. Η εργασία καταλήγει στην παρουσίαση ενός λειτουργικού πρωτοτύπου εκπαιδευτικής πλατφόρμας, το οποίο συνδυάζει την οργάνωση μαθησιακού περιεχομένου, την παρακολούθηση προόδου και την εφαρμογή βασικών κανόνων προσαρμογής. Η παρούσα υλοποίηση δεν περιλαμβάνει πειραματική αξιολόγηση με πραγματικούς μαθητές και, επομένως, δεν εξάγει συμπεράσματα για τη μαθησιακή αποτελεσματικότητα της πλατφόρμας σε πραγματικές συνθήκες. Ωστόσο, θέτει τη βάση για μελλοντική επέκταση, εμπλουτισμό του περιεχομένου, πιο σύνθετη αξιοποίηση learning analytics και αξιολόγηση της χρήσης του συστήματος σε πραγματικό εκπαιδευτικό περιβάλλον.

title: The Therma Neuron A Complete, Reproducible Account of Homeostatic, Metabolic, and Consolidative Neuron Architectures
abstract: A complete, reproducible account of the Therma Neuron: A metabolic activation whose thermal state gates gradient flow, conserves total gradient mass via ThermaGradient, and stores blocked signal in a Hebbian associative overlay. Validated on Permuted MNIST (3 seeds, 0.0089 forgetting), CIFAR-100 (FC-only 0.0731, full conv+FC vault 0.0863, tuned champion 0.0543), and DeepSeek-Coder 1.3B (Python → JavaScript → C++, negative forgetting). Includes NecroGraft full-rank weight expansion for zero-forgetting adaptation, Spiky Neural Cluster forward-only domain gating validated on MedMCQA/MMLU, the optimizer requirement (AdamW where nothing is blocked, SGD momentum where the mask is active), and a full debugging log with root causes and fixes for every failure encountered. Every number is from an actual run.

title: Pengaruh Ekosistem Komunikasi Pemasaran Berbasis Kecerdasan Buatan terhadap Perilaku Konsumen
abstract: Kecerdasan buatan telah mengubah komunikasi pemasaran digital, tetapi pengaruh khusus interaktivitas dan personalisasi terhadap perilaku konsumen belum sepenuhnya dipahami. Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh interaktivitas dan personalisasi berbasis kecerdasan buatan terhadap keterlibatan konsumen dan niat beli pada 190 pengguna platform digital berbasis kecerdasan buatan di Indonesia. Data dikumpulkan melalui survei daring dengan teknik purposive sampling dan dianalisis menggunakan pemodelan persamaan struktural kuadrat terkecil parsial. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa interaktivitas berpengaruh positif kuat terhadap keterlibatan konsumen (koefisien = 1,081), sedangkan personalisasi berpengaruh negatif terhadap keterlibatan (koefisien = -0,382), yang menunjukkan paradoks personalisasi dan privasi. Namun, personalisasi berpengaruh langsung positif terhadap niat beli (koefisien = 0,325). title: Making a Seven-Decade Policy Collection Navigable: Domain-Adapted Sentence Embeddings and a Coverage-Aware Topic-Alignment Protocol for Chinese Government Work Reports
abstract: Chinese government work reports form a large civic archive whose formulaic language and uneven historical coverage complicate thematic organization. We index 6,839 central, provincial, and prefectural reports spanning 1954–2025 and analyze 6,316 retained documents and 2.39 million sentences from 1980–2025. We develop EnvTextSim, a Chinese sentence encoder adapted with an adaptive circle loss to an author-defined environmental taxonomy, and a coverage-aware topic-evaluation protocol based on Hungarian soft alignment. On distantly labelled test sentences, intra-/inter-topic cosine similarity is 0.994/0.016, compared with 0.797/0.768 for text2vec-base-chinese and 0.786/0.826 for bge-large-zh-v1.5. In a guided BERTopic run, the adapted encoder recovers 13 of 14 taxonomy topics, compared with seven for text2vec. These results measure taxonomy consistency: training, topic guidance, and alignment all reuse the same dictionary. Keyword masking reduces EnvTextSim’s nearest-centroid accuracy from 0.993 to 0.471, showing substantial dependence on the supervision vocabulary. Separately, dictionary-based panels describe environmental attention and first observed textual appearances across administrative levels. Removing eight broad keywords preserves the overall provincial attention pattern (r = 0.966) but changes several topic-specific timing estimates. Retrieval examples illustrate topical access without establishing ranking quality or usability. The accompanying labelled sentences, analysis panels, taxonomy, and reproducibility materials support further collection research and independent validation.

title: TabGift: A Context-Efficient Foundation Model for Tabular Data Generation
abstract: Tabular data generation aims to synthesize realistic samples from limited observations while faithfully capturing the underlying data distribution. Tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained on diverse tabular tasks and adapted through in-context learning, have demonstrated strong predictive capabilities, suggesting the potential of extending this paradigm to tabular data generation. However, the strong predictive performance of TFMs often relies on sufficiently large context sets, whereas tabular generation is typically needed precisely when target data are scarce. Extending the foundation-model paradigm to generation therefore requires reliable distribution inference from only a limited context. To this end, we propose TabGift, a context-efficient tabular foundation model enabling both efficient distribution modeling and effective generation from only a few context samples. TabGift maps heterogeneous tables into a shared latent space with a pretrained tabular encoder, where an in-context diffusion model learns to denoise latent samples conditioned on a small set of clean examples. This design transfers generative priors across datasets and enables distribution inference from limited context, while a lightweight dataset-specific MLP decoder maps generated representations back to the original data space. Experiments on 7 classification and 11 regression datasets show that TabGift consistently outperforms representative baselines in synthetic data quality, with particularly strong gains under limited-context settings, while achieving substantially faster adaptation and generation.

title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model
abstract: Video-to-robot pipelines for quadrupedal imitation insert a learned lifting stage, either a monocular depth model or a per-clip 3D reconstruction, to recover the one axis a side-view camera cannot see. We present CopyQuad, which omits that stage and pins the missing axis to the robot's own stance width instead. The setting is side-view footage of sagittally dominated motion, where limb motion is almost entirely in the image plane. A frozen 2D keypoint detector and a fixed analytic retargeting then turn a single uncalibrated clip into a robot reference whose foot targets are reachable by construction, so no per-clip trajectory optimization is needed. One phase-indexed reward structure, whose only per-behavior freedom is three scalars from a shared sweep, learns a dog walk, a horse walk, a horse trot and two non-periodic gestures, all deployed zero-shot on hardware. We then measure what omitting the axis costs. In a training-free rigidity test, a video depth model varies the distance between the animal's hips by $40$ to $107\%$ of its own mean and a single-image metric model by $22$ to $58\%$, though that distance cannot move. Motion capture puts the true lateral paw travel of a dog walk at $4.5$ cm peak to peak, a mean deviation near $1.4$ cm against the $3.5$ cm of lateral foot error our policies already leave, so the discarded axis sits below the pipeline's resolution. Depth repaired to feasibility never beats the constant, and the unrepaired estimates put the robot on the ground.

title: Look Back to Move Forward: Learning to Revisit for Agentic Compositional Image Generation
abstract: Text-to-image models have made remarkable progress in visual fidelity and instruction following, yet complex compositional generation remains challenging. Existing agentic approaches address this limitation through iterative generation and editing, adapting their actions based on interaction history. However, they typically fix the continuation state (i.e., the image from which refinement proceeds) to the latest image. Since iterative editing is not necessarily monotonic, the agent may continue refining from the latest image even when it has already degraded. In this work, we introduce GenRevisit, an agentic framework that extends action selection to joint continuation-state and action selection. The agent can not only use interaction history to adjust editing instructions but also select an image candidate to edit, jointly deciding where to continue from and how to refine. We train GenRevisit with SFT followed by agentic reinforcement learning. To address the coarse credit assignment of final outcome reward in GRPO, which assigns the same trajectory-level advantage to all actions, we further propose Normalized Action Credit Assignment (NACA) to redistribute positive advantage according to each action's contribution to reducing the remaining objective. On GenEval2, GenRevisit achieves GM scores of 84.3 and 74.4 with Qwen-Image-2512 and Z-Image-Turbo, surpassing the strongest baselines using the same generators by 12.7 and 10.9 points respectively. GenRevisit achieves state-of-the-art performance on GenEval, GenEval++, and GenEval2 among baselines.

title: Perbandingan Support Vector Machine dan K-Nearest Neighbor pada Klasifikasi Emosi Tweet
abstract: Klasifikasi emosi pada tweet berbahasa Indonesia sulit dilakukan karena teks media sosial sering memakai bahasa tidak baku. Penelitian ini membandingkan Support Vector Machine dan K-Nearest Neighbor melalui delapan konfigurasi yang mengombinasikan term frequency-inverse document frequency atau bigram, synthetic minority oversampling, dan penyetelan grid search. Eksperimen menggunakan 4.403 tweet berlabel manual dalam lima kelas emosi, dengan 90% data latih dan 10% data uji. Teks menjalani case folding, cleaning, dan normalisasi. Kinerja dievaluasi melalui validasi silang sepuluh lipatan dan confusion matrix. Support Vector Machine dengan term frequency-inverse document frequency, oversampling, dan penyetelan menghasilkan akurasi terbaik sebesar 76,04% dan F1-score 76,19%. K-Nearest Neighbor mencapai akurasi 54,08% dan F1-score 48,61%. Term frequency-inverse document frequency secara konsisten mengungguli bigram, sedangkan pengaruh oversampling berbeda menurut algoritma.

title: The Role of AI In Startup Resource Optimization: A Content-Analytic Study Using Chi-Square, ANOVA and Linear Regression
abstract: Startups operate using a limited amount of financial, human, temporal and technological resources. The effective application of these scarce resources determines the survival and growth prospects of a startup. Artificial Intelligence, referred to as AI is increasingly being leveraged to perform tasks look at business data predict demand assist in decision-making and enhance customer service. This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence on the optimization of a startup’s resources. The research methodology uses a set of ten articles published in 2024-2026 in Bloomberg, Fortune and the Indianapolis Business Journal periodicals. For each article we identified the resource that was emphasized assessed the level of Artificial Intelligence utilization and determined the presence of five resource‑optimization areas. These areas include cost efficiency, time efficiency, employee productivity, decision‑making and operational efficiency. We applied a set of statistical instruments including chi‑square tests, one‑way ANOVA and simple linear regression to analyse the data. We present the results of our findings using bar graphs.

title: Root Hitting for Multiparameter Feature Families under Cube Coefficients
abstract: Random transition sets control whether small changes in algorithm parameters can cause discontinuous losses. Bounds along a single parameter curve do not determine the probability of a transition somewhere in a multidimensional neighborhood. We prove that, for a nonvanishing feature map whose normalization is $L$-Lipschitz on an $m$-dimensional parameter ball of radius $r$, a coefficient law dominated by $A$ times the uniform cube law has root-hitting probability at most $\min\{1,CALr\sqrt m\}$. The bound is independent of the feature dimension and permits arbitrary orientation relative to the cube. A linear feature family gives a matching parameter-dimension order. The proof controls exponential moments on unnormalized hyperplane slices through product tilting and a classical projection-density bound, then chains over the feature image. An isotropic log-concave Laplace construction has hitting probability of order at least $Lr m$, separating the multidimensional conclusion from one-dimensional log-concave flux bounds. A finite-net argument yields uniform boundary counts and a full-information online-learning guarantee without a bounded Pfaffian complexity assumption. Preprint; not peer reviewed.

title: What Counts as a Control? A Scaffold Effect Is a Contrast Conditional on What Was Held Fixed, the 2026 Controlled Studies Each Held Something Different, and Only a Declared Spend Interval Makes a Harness Claim Refutable
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. A language-model agent is a model wrapped in a harness that builds its context, exposes its tools, decides when to retry and when to stop. Several 2026 studies set out to measure how much the harness matters relative to the model, holding the model and the tasks fixed, and their answers do not stack: within-model gaps of 0 to 8 points on one terminal benchmark alongside a 40-fold spread in tokens per solved task, 8.5 to 13 points on a coding subset, and up to 28 points on a question-answering benchmark. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that these are not noisy estimates of one quantity. A harness effect is a contrast between two systems conditional on a control set - what was held fixed and what was left free - and a readout, and each study fixed something different: native budget controls, a shared step cap, an attempt count, or nothing at all. The paper argues four points. A cap is not a spend, so a matched ceiling leaves consumption free and lets a harness win by spending. Accuracy is purchasable with attempts, time and retries, so a harness claim with no declared budget excludes no observation. Model and harness interact, so a harness main effect is a property of the model grid. And run-to-run variance is of the same order as many reported gaps. The paper consolidates the measured values in a table and a figure, separates three questions that call for three different controls, states a decision procedure as an algorithm, and names the studies that would settle what remains open.

title: A Comprehensive Study of Implicit-Aware Methods for Generative Aspect-Category-Opinion-Sentiment Extraction
abstract: Aspects and opinions in reviews are often left unstated, and these implicit cases remain the hardest part of Aspect-Category-Opinion-Sentiment (ACOS) quadruple extraction. We reimplement the generative GEN-SCL-NAT model on a T5-Base backbone and add two modifications aimed at those cases. Instead of a single overall score, we report results separately for the four ways an aspect and an opinion can be written or left out. Seen this way, one modification helps on implicit aspects and hurts on implicit opinions, while the overall score barely changes. Gains appear only where either the aspect or the opinion still remains in the sentence. Where neither is written, nothing improves beyond the variation we see between training runs.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Semantically Consistent Visual Features via a Simple 3D Prior
abstract: Visual features extracted from vision models like DINOv2 or Stable Diffusion enable high quality semantic correspondence between images. However, such features exhibit documented limitations that hinder accurate correspondence estimation such as the inability to disambiguate the left from right for categories exhibiting symmetries or repeated parts. Previous attempts to improve these features rely on using supervised data such as annotated keypoint pairs or camera pose information, or make restrictive topological assumptions, such as modelling the object of interest as a 3D sphere. We introduce a new self-supervised approach that allows us to learn features for topologically complex object categories using a simple prior. Instead of relying on an expensive instance-level analysis by synthesis pipeline, our approach makes use of contrastive learning and distribution matching at the global dataset-level to learn the coarse shape and appearance of a category. Combined with additional geometric losses, this enables us to replicate the global and local statistics of visual features which match those that are extracted from real images. Quantitative results are presented across several challenging object categories, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Amortised adaptive importance sampling
abstract: Monte Carlo sampling algorithms aim to produce samples from a target distribution with a given unnormalised probability density function. The high cost of running Monte Carlo algorithms, with many simulation steps or particles needed to obtain a good empirical approximation to the target, can be reduced by introducing learnable components into the sampler -- a form of amortisation. Once these components are trained, amortised samplers can produce high-quality samples with less computation at sampling time than training-free algorithms would require. We propose an amortised sampler built upon the framework of adaptive importance sampling -- a hierarchical importance sampling procedure where the proposal is iteratively adapted. Our amortised adaptive importance sampling algorithm fits a lightweight neural network that adapts the proposal using information obtained over the course of sampling. By training our sampler over many different targets taken from the same family of distributions, we obtain a sampler that can adapt to a specific target at sampling time without a priori access to the target's parameters. We show that our procedure can efficiently sample from targets within the family the sampler was trained on, giving improvements over target-specific amortised samplers and training-free adaptive importance sampling algorithms. We also explore the potential for generalisation, where the trained sampler is used to sample from targets outwith its training family.

evidence.title: Amortised adaptive importance sampling
evidence.abstract: Monte Carlo sampling algorithms aim to produce samples from a target distribution with a given unnormalised probability density function. The high cost of running Monte Carlo algorithms, with many simulation steps or particles needed to obtain a good empirical approximation to the target, can be reduced by introducing learnable components into the sampler -- a form of amortisation. Once these components are trained, amortised samplers can produce high-quality samples with less computation at sampling time than training-free algorithms would require. We propose an amortised sampler built upon the framework of adaptive importance sampling -- a hierarchical importance sampling procedure where the proposal is iteratively adapted. Our amortised adaptive importance sampling algorithm fits a lightweight neural network that adapts the proposal using information obtained over the course of sampling. By training our sampler over many different targets taken from the same family of distributions, we obtain a sampler that can adapt to a specific target at sampling time without a priori access to the target's parameters. We show that our procedure can efficiently sample from targets within the family the sampler was trained on, giving improvements over target-specific amortised samplers and training-free adaptive importance sampling algorithms. We also explore the potential for generalisation, where the trained sampler is used to sample from targets outwith its training family.

title: Ontology-Based Post-Coordinated Expression Assembly: from Clinical Narrative to Queryable Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Clinical oncology documentation records decisive information in free text, where it remains readable but not retrievable at scale, leaving cohort identification dependent on incomplete diagnostic codes or manual review. The current standard, coding individual terms, captures what a document mentions, not what it asserts: meaning lies in how those terms relate to one another. We present a method for deriving queryable knowledge graphs from clinical narratives, conforming to the Extended Grammar of SNOMED CT across multiple ontologies. The method specifies how entities should be annotated and related. It defines five relation classes, each bound to a construction rule that assembles the entities and relations into post-coordinated expressions. A deterministic implementation, UNIGRAPHE, applies those rules to construct knowledge graphs from annotated text. Applied to expert-annotated real-world oncology documentation, UNIGRAPHE reconstructed 5,299 annotations into 2,196 post-coordinated expressions and shows that relation structure is the missing piece to make clinical narrative formally queryable.

title: Magic-Free Certification of Logical Error Rates in Universal Fault-Tolerant Circuits
abstract: As quantum hardware enters the fault-tolerant regime, algorithms are beginning to be executed on encoded qubits, yet scalable certification of how well they run remains an open problem. Here we introduce magic-free certification, a certification protocol for universal fault-tolerant circuits that consumes no magic, the resource that generally places them beyond efficient classical simulation and is by far the most expensive element of a fault-tolerant computation. The protocol is code- and decoder-agnostic, runs interleaved with the target circuit on the same device, and has a sample complexity that grows linearly with the number of logical qubits and non-Clifford gates while remaining decoupled from the logical error rate itself. Given a predefined error tolerance $p_L^*$, the protocol determines at a chosen confidence level whether the device executes the target circuit at a logical error rate below $p_L^*$. The method relies on trap circuits, copies of the target with every magic state replaced by a stabilizer state, whose outcomes are deterministic and which, being indistinguishable from the target to stochastic Pauli noise, fail at the same rate. We illustrate the protocol in Steane-code simulations of a magic state injection gadget and a quantum Fourier transform.

title: When Participant Disjoint Validation Is Not Enough to Establish Generalization in Parkinson's Gait Classification
abstract: Participant-disjoint cross-validation prevents direct participant overlap, but it may still produce optimistic estimates when acquisition site and diagnosis are structurally dependent. We examined Parkinson's disease classification using 159 pressure-walkway summary features from 133 WearGait-PD participants, including 65 participants with Parkinson's disease and 68 controls. The cohort was non-factorial: two sites contained only one diagnostic group, whereas VA-Seattle was the only site containing both groups. In repeated participant-level nested cross-validation, site alone achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.955 plus or minus 0.003, exceeding the gait-feature model (0.882 plus or minus 0.014). Under the evaluated logistic-regression pipelines, adding gait features to site, age, and sex produced no measurable improvement in pooled discrimination. More site-controlled evaluations produced lower and imprecise estimates: VA-Seattle same-site AUC was 0.668 (95% bootstrap confidence interval 0.477 to 0.836), and the JHOC + Bayview-to-VA-Seattle transport stress test achieved 0.576 (0.375 to 0.770). Supporting within-diagnosis site-prediction and site-conditioned permutation analyses showed that the gait representation retained substantial acquisition-site structure. These findings indicate that participant-disjoint pooled validation did not isolate disease-related discrimination from site-associated variation. They encourage careful examination of site-label dependence and, where possible, support for pooled results through within-site or independent validation before broader claims are made about generalization across institutions.

title: Sequential optimization for orbital-optimized variational quantum eigensolvers
abstract: Orbital optimization within the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) framework is useful for improving active-space quality and accurately capturing electron correlation with shallow quantum circuits. The orbital-optimized unitary coupled cluster (OO-UCC) method [W. Mizukami et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 033421 (2020)], in its original formulation, employs the orbital gradient and Hessian in a Newton--Laphson procedure. In this study, we propose sequential orbital-optimized unitary coupled cluster doubles (SOO-UCCD), extending the gradient-free sequential minimal optimization approach [K. M. Nakanishi et al., Phys. Rev. Res. 2, 043158 (2020)] to orbital rotation parameters. Based on the frequency structure implied by the algebraic properties of the orbital rotation generators, our method determines each orbital rotation angle from a nine-point energy profile. The energy landscape is evaluated by classically transforming the Hamiltonian integrals and contracting them with the reduced density matrices already measured for the VQE energy evaluation. This allows for orbital optimization without evaluating the orbital gradient or Hessian. By building on the core benefits of the OO-UCC framework, our method provides a gradient-free and hyperparameter-free orbital-optimization procedure. State-vector simulations for LiH in the STO-3G basis show that SOO-UCCD reproduces UCCSD-level accuracy along the bond-stretching curve and exhibits macro-iteration convergence comparable to that of L-BFGS-based orbital optimization.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Business Management: A Conceptual Study of Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly discussed as a core element of contemporary business management, yet the literature remains scattered across technical, managerial, and ethical perspectives. This conceptual study synthesises twenty recent scholarly and repository sources to examine how AI is understood to reshape management practice, which opportunities it creates, and which challenges accompany its adoption. A thematic reading of the sources shows consistent attention to improved decision-making, process automation, customer engagement, strategic innovation, and functional applications in human resources, supply chains, finance, and information systems. The same sources also point to ethical risks such as algorithmic bias and weak transparency, to data privacy and security concerns, to workforce disruption, and to cost, skills, and infrastructure constraints. Building on these themes, the paper proposes an integrated framework in which technological capability, organisational readiness, and responsible governance jointly determine whether AI delivers sustained value. The study concludes that AI is best understood as a tool for augmenting human judgement rather than replacing it, and it outlines implications for managers, policymakers, and future researchers.

title: Atlas of the 222 NPN classes of 4-variable Boolean functions in three bases (AIG, MIG, XAG): circuit size, formula size, gap and structural invariants
abstract: One table, 222 rows: every NPN class of 4-variable Boolean functions, with its minimum circuit size (opt), minimum formula size (tree, fan-out 1) and gap = tree − opt in three bases: AIG (2-input AND, free inversions), MIG (3-input majority, free inversions and constants) and XAG (2-input AND and XOR, free inversions), each counted in gates of its own basis. Twelve structural columns computed from the truth table alone follow: NP and strict self-duality, NP stabilizer and orbit sizes, NPN class size, ANF degree, essential variables, canalization, minimum weight and minimum ANF term count over the class, and whether some member is monotone. In this table 93, 168 and 218 classes have gap 0 in AIG, MIG and XAG; the maximum gap is 6, 3 and 1; 82 classes have gap 0 in all three bases, and one class, 0x1668, has a positive gap in all three. How to verify. verify_atlas.py (Python 3, no dependencies) checks without a solver that the rows are exactly the 222 NPN classes, recomputes all twelve structural columns, and checks gap = tree − opt in each basis. Limits. opt comes from SAT-based exact synthesis; its unsatisfiable side is a solver answer and is not DRAT-certified class by class here. tree comes from exact dynamic programs over formulas. The MIG columns agree in distribution with Tables I and II of Soeken et al. (DATE 2016), which do not publish per-class values; the XAG columns agree class by class with the n = 4 restriction of the optimal5 and Lflib5 (IWLS 2019) tables, Lflib5 counting formula length in gates. The circuits and formulas behind opt and tree are not part of this record. Exhaustive for n = 4 only. Measured frontier (version 1.1). In AIG the tree column was also checked class by class with a SAT encoder in formula mode. frontier_summary.csv gives, for each class, the run that decided it, and frontier/runs/ inside the zip keeps every run, with the cap per solver call of each run file listed in README.md: 203 classes pass, 2 are trivial, and the 17 classes with tree_aig ≥ 12 are undecided, the unsatisfiable side having run out of time at 21,600 s per solver call. For those 17, tree_aig rests on the dynamic program alone. An undecided row is a timeout, not evidence either way. The atlas table itself is unchanged from version 1.0. Data under CC BY 4.0; verify_atlas.py under MIT.

title: Identifiability of Neural Learning Rules Under Sparse and Noisy Observations: A Virtual-Experiment Study
abstract: Backpropagation cannot run in the brain as literally implemented: it requires weight transport, non-local error signals, and strict alternating forward and backward phases. Local alternatives have been proposed for a decade but rarely tested against the data experiments produce: few neurons, noisy calcium imaging, sparse time points. We implement six candidate rules behind one shared interface, verify each against known theoretical equivalences, and train all six under one matched online regime across two tasks and three architectures. A virtual experiment then subsamples units, adds calcium-imaging-like noise calibrated against real Allen Institute recordings, and sparsifies timepoints. Classifiers identifying which rule produced a run's observables top out near 54% six-way (chance 16.7%), with a wide bootstrap 95% interval of [36.4%, 60.6%]. Five of the six rules split into two families, {backpropagation, predictive coding} against {feedback alignment, direct feedback alignment, burst-dependent plasticity}, and that split is far easier to call: 98.5% in distribution, 95.6% on an architecture never seen in training, and 81.1% on an unseen task family, reproduced across three separately trained sweeps. Behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity (BTSP) separates from the other five at 100% precision and recall, and 122 of 128 conditions survive a grid-wide multiple-comparisons correction. The discriminability spectrum shows why the coarse question is the tractable one. It is dominated by one direction in all 256 conditions across two independently trained sweeps, and that direction is the family contrast itself (minimum alignment 0.9993). At three timepoints and 3% of units, family membership remains recoverable at 89-91% while individual rule identity falls to 15-17%, at or below chance. The signature survives controls for learning speed and pooled learning rates, and a log-normal weight initialisation matched to real MICrONS synapse statistics, and is carried mainly by population activity variance, not early weight change. We turn this into testable predictions for real recordings.

title: BanglaMobileABSA-AT: A Fine-Grained Re-annotated Dataset for Aspect-Term-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: BanglaMobileABSA-AT is a fine-grained re-annotated dataset for aspect-term-based sentiment analysis of Bangla mobile-phone reviews. The dataset is derived from the 975-review Mobile_phone_ABSA subset of the BANGLA-ABSA dataset. Each accepted annotation records the exact aspect term appearing in the review, its normalized canonical aspect, and its sentiment label as Positive, Negative, or Neutral. The final dataset contains 975 reviews and 1,646 aspect instances across 18 canonical aspects. Of the 975 reviews, 960 contain at least one accepted aspect annotation and 15 contain no accepted aspect. The sentiment distribution is 720 Positive, 874 Negative, and 52 Neutral instances. The release includes the master workbook, review-level annotations, flattened aspect instances with character offsets, fixed train/validation/test split metadata, and the exact train, validation, and test files used for the reported experiments. The fixed split contains 780 training reviews, 97 validation reviews, and 98 test reviews, generated using seed 42. This dataset is a re-annotation of the Mobile_phone_ABSA subset of BANGLA-ABSA. Attribution to the original dataset and its authors must be preserved.

title: CLIP-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection with Machine Unlearning and Negative Learning Strategies for Noisy Labels Learning
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs), due to their over-parameterization and memorization capacity, are prone to fitting incorrect labels in training data, which can substantially degrade their performance. Consequently, LNL has attracted increasing attention. Popular LNL methods select potentially clean samples for reliable supervision while applying robust techniques to the remaining samples to mitigate the adverse effects of label noise. However, when sample selection relies solely on the continuously updated classifier, the classifier may gradually memorize incorrect labels during training, and the resulting biased predictions can further affect subsequent sample selection, leading to a self-reinforcing confirmation bias. To address this issue, we propose CAMN, a CLIP-guided adaptive sample selection with machine unlearning and negative learning strategies for noisy labels learning. Specifically, CAMN introduces a pretrained vision language model CLIP as an external semantic prior independent of the task-specific classifier to perform preliminary noise-aware sample selection. The resulting selections are then integrated with an adaptive and balanced sample selection strategy to provide more reliable samples for robust learning. CLIP provides an independent external semantic prior for reducing classifier-induced bias, while the selection results from the trained DNN complements CLIP-based zero-shot selection by reducing over-reliance on its predictions and promoting more balanced sample selection. After selection, CAMN further incorporates a machine unlearning mechanism and a negative learning strategy as regularizers, reducing the persistent influence of noisy labels on DNN and further enhancing its robustness. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of CAMN across diverse noise settings, including synthetic and Web-crawled noisy datasets.

title: "DySTI-AD: Public Multivariate Time-Series Benchmark Datasets for Anomaly Detection"
abstract: "This dataset collection contains five publicly available multivariate time-series anomaly detection benchmarks used in the experimental evaluation of DySTI-AD: MSL, SMAP, SMD, PSM, and MBA. These benchmarks cover multiple monitoring scenarios, including spacecraft telemetry, server monitoring, service monitoring, and electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings. The collection includes time-series observations organized into training and testing subsets, together with the available anomaly labels for evaluation.The datasets exhibit diverse temporal patterns, heterogeneous variable dependencies, abnormal fluctuations, and potentially non-stationary behaviors. They support the evaluation of unsupervised anomaly detection methods under different data characteristics and anomaly patterns. This collection is provided to facilitate access to the benchmark files used in the DySTI-AD study and to support reproducibility and comparative evaluation.All five benchmarks originate from previously published public data sources and are not newly collected datasets. The original creators, relevant references, dataset versions, and applicable reuse conditions should be acknowledged in the accompanying documentation."

title: Recast Navigation
abstract: This chapter serves as a practical guide to working with the Recast Navigation library to manage your AI’s nav-mesh representation of the game world. The source code to Recast is both freely available and frequently used due to its inclusion in Unreal, Unity, and many other engines. This guide will go over how the nav-mesh assets were managed in published games including creation, metrics, annotation, and dynamic updates.

title: AI under Lockdown
abstract: Restricting AI navigation to certain areas of a continuous game world is a notion often referred to as “tethering.” There are many different reasons why you might want to confine non-player characters (NPCs) to a region instead of letting them move freely. Often, system design needs to prevent players from gathering too much “aggro” as they run through the world. In games where the AI cost on hardware resources is a concern, it is also possible to use tethering as a performance control measure. Level design can also be at play, in cases where NPCs with certain abilities are not adapted to some parts of a level. How to achieve NPC tethering in your game will largely depend on the goals you are pursuing. There is no silver bullet. This chapter will go through a variety of different methods for tethering agents and detail what they are good for, along with the issues that come with them.

This chapter will go through a variety of different methods for tethering agents and detail what they are good for, along with the issues that come with them.

title: VeriRouter: Towards Verifiable LLM Routing
abstract: Large language model (LLM) routers are increasingly deployed to optimize quality, latency, and cost through dynamic model selection and request rewriting. However, a compromised router can cause ineligible selection on the control plane, unendorsed rewriting or unfaithful relay on the data plane, undermining LLM routing integrity. We present VeriRouter, a verifiable LLM routing framework. Under an endorsed public context binding a private semantic index and rewrite banks, VeriRouter combines ZK proofs with a provider-issued serving certificate to establish integrity across both planes while keeping the router's private routing assets hidden from clients. For model selection, we design an efficient ZK proof for semantic search. For rewriting, local checks enforce message preservation and additions from committed banks. On real-world workloads, VeriRouter's model-selection and rewrite proofs average 21.92~s and 4.24~s, yielding 1,307$\times$ and 101$\times$ speedups over the fastest completing baselines. Relative to serving without verification, VeriRouter adds only 4.08 s under per-turn selection and 0.11 s under session-pinned selection.

title: HybridDualPathNet: Cross-Fusion Attention of EfficientNetV2 and Swin Transformer for Brain MRI Classification of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Disease
abstract: Separating Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), and Healthy Controls (HC) using structural MRI remains challenging because disease signatures overlap and model performance can be strongly affected by data partitioning. We present HybridDualPathNet, a hybrid architecture combining EfficientNetV2-S for local features and Swin-Tiny for global context through a Cross-Fusion Attention (CFA) module. We evaluate the model in two experiments. First, on the Kaggle APD-3-Class dataset using an image-level split, the model achieves 98.25% accuracy. Second, on a combined Kaggle and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset containing 17,859 slices, we use a per-source split with patient-wise separation for ADNI subjects. In this setting, the model achieves 73.37% standard accuracy and a macro AUC of 0.880. Source-stratified evaluation reveals a substantial domain gap, with 91.2% accuracy on Kaggle test images and 59.2% on ADNI test images. Temperature scaling reduces expected calibration error from 0.130 to 0.015, while split-conformal prediction achieves 89.5% coverage. Saliency analyses using Grad-CAM++, Integrated Gradients, and occlusion indicate that model activations concentrate on brain tissue. These results highlight the importance of patient-level separation, cross-dataset evaluation, and uncertainty estimation when assessing MRI classification systems. The findings also show that strong performance on a single dataset does not necessarily translate to reliable generalization across imaging cohorts.

title: Calibrating AlphaFold confidence scores for interface quality
abstract: AlphaFold confidence scores are widely used to rank protein complex predictions and to select subsets of models for downstream applications. Although these scores provide strong discriminatory power for distinguishing prediction quality, their numerical values were never intended to represent the probability that a prediction satisfies a given structural quality criterion. In this work, we calibrate commonly used confidence scores to estimate the probability that a predicted complex exceeds a chosen threshold of DockQ, an established measure of interface quality. On antibody-antigen and general multimer datasets, post-hoc isotonic calibration consistently improves agreement between predicted probabilities and observed DockQ success rates while preserving the underlying score ordering. The calibrated probabilities also provide more accurate estimates of the fraction of selected models expected to pass a given structural quality threshold. Although the mapping is fitted within a given prediction distribution and therefore transfers imperfectly across prediction domains, we show that reliable estimates are recovered from a small number of labeled target-domain samples. Because the calibration is entirely post hoc and requires no underlying AlphaFold model fine-tuning, it provides a straightforward and customizable way to convert existing model quality rankings into calibrated probabilities of passing a chosen structural quality threshold.

title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization
abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards commonly assigns one sequence advantage to an entire response. This outcome-level signal distinguishes overall response quality but leaves changes in visual-evidence use across generated tokens implicit. We introduce VAttnPO (Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization), which uses answer-conditioned visual attention to refine token-level credit while preserving the verifier-derived trajectory-mean advantage. A frozen old policy constructs a visual reference by teacher forcing the known correct answer and produces a visual distribution for each rollout token. VAttnPO measures their agreement in visual-attention space using Jensen--Shannon divergence, rather than reading guidance from teacher output-token distributions or introducing an attention-matching objective. Trajectory centering, relative-position weighting, and credit balancing turn this agreement into a zero-mean, position-aware correction to the GRPO sequence advantage. Token intervention, visual-index permutation, and trajectory analysis provide diagnostic evidence linking this signal to model behavior, visual correspondence, and generation position. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, VAttnPO raises six-task image AVE from 70.97 with GRPO to 73.50 and scores higher on every reported structured, video, and MME metric. Gains over GRPO also hold on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3-8B-Instruct.

title: CircuitBreak: Pruning a Sparse Safety Circuit of Neurons
abstract: White-box neuron pruning has shown that refusal in large language models (LLMs) can depend on a small, removable set of feed-forward (FFN) channels. Existing attacks either need carefully paired ``twin'' prompts or score each neuron in isolation. Pruning also has an unavoidable capability cost, so over-removal compounds the loss. TwinBreak removes $1\%$--$5\%$ of parameters and NeuroStrike removes $0.3\%$--$0.7\%$ of neurons in targeted layers. We model safety as a small \emph{circuit} whose neurons contribute jointly rather than independently. We propose \textsc{CircuitBreak}, a neuron-pruning attack that greedily searches for a sparse set of FFN neurons whose joint ablation flips a refusal readout. \textsc{CircuitBreak} re-scores every candidate after the neurons already removed and needs no twin prompts. On ten instruction-tuned models, the greedy search converges after removing $29$--$150$ neurons ($0.0066\%$--$0.0388\%$ of the MLP). The pruned models raise the attack success rate from $2.24\%$/$7.35\%$ to $87.54\%$/$87.54\%$ on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and from $8.95\%$/$5.43\%$ to $88.50\%$/$88.18\%$ on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, as judged by Llama Guard 3 8B on StrongREJECT.

title: Commerce Core Expansion: Auditing Small-Model Adaptation for Product Matching and Attribute Extraction
abstract: Small language models could support several product-understanding operations within a retailer’s infrastructure, but evidence of task accuracy is easily con-founded with evidence of generalization or serving efficiency. We study QLoRA adaptation of Qwen3-1.7B for query–product relevance, listing identity, functional relation, technical compatibility, and brand/color extraction. We reconstruct the experiments from committed data, checkpoint histories, training logs, prediction records, and serving traces, and release an offline audit that regenerates the quanti-tative analysis. On a common 200-listing extraction sample, the dedicated adapter attains brand F1 of 1.000 and color F1 of 0.955 under the recorded permissive matching rule; the latter exceeds the strongest tested API comparator by 1.38 per-centage points. This is a descriptive result: two evaluation texts also occur in training, and missing paired outputs prevent a significance claim. Matching re-sults expose a different problem. Adapter and API relevance scores use different samples; a single-token relevance adapter reaches 0.5115 accuracy but only 0.436 macro-F1; and 25 of 28 functional-relation test rows reuse training scenarios. A checkpoint sweep further exposes that test partition to model selection. We for-malize the information required for comparable evaluations, demonstrate scorer counterexamples, and bound the paired correctness uncertainty recoverable from aggregate extraction counts. Historical load tests contain no completed inference requests. A separate RunPod follow-up adds paired development evaluations un-der two prompt interfaces, a text-extraction comparator and bounded HTTP serv-ing measurements; these do not establish final-test generalization or production cost advantage. The evidence supports promising narrow extraction behavior and a reproducible account of evaluation failure modes, rather than universal superior-ity or a production-ready horizontal model.

title: RANKING ALGORITHMS FOR MEDICAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS BASED ON NOMINAL DATA
abstract: The rapid expansion of electronic health records (EHRs), hospital information systems, clinical decision-support platforms, and digital patient registries has increased the need for reliable algorithms capable of processing heterogeneous clinical information. A substantial proportion of medical information is nominal rather than numerical or ordinal. Examples include diagnosis categories, medication classes, symptom types, admission reasons, procedure codes, departments, blood groups, and other categorical attributes. Nominal categories have no inherent mathematical order; therefore, assigning arbitrary numerical codes to them may introduce artificial relationships and distort the results of statistical or machine-learning models. This article examines algorithms for solving ranking problems in medical information systems when the underlying information is nominal. The methodological framework considers categorical-data representation, frequency-based ranking, probabilistic ranking, multinomial logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, support-vector approaches, learning-to-rank methods, and rank aggregation. Particular attention is given to one-hot encoding and other appropriate representations of nominal variables, because preserving the absence of ordinal meaning is fundamental to valid modelling. Published medical informatics studies demonstrate that ranking can support emergency triage, retrieval of relevant EHR information, clinical prediction, and prioritization of patient-related information. For example, a learning-to-rank study involving 90 EHR notes reported an AUC-ROC of 0.940 for ranking candidate medical terms, while a structured-record relevance-ranking study evaluated 1,010 medications and 2,913 problems from 99 patients. These published results demonstrate the practical feasibility of ranking approaches in healthcare, although performance depends strongly on data quality, outcome definition, validation, calibration, and clinical context. The article proposes a general algorithmic framework for nominal-data ranking that combines categorical encoding, clinically meaningful feature construction, model training, ranking-score generation, validation, and human oversight.

title: Legal Discipline of Data Procurement and Corporate Governance in Generative AI Development: A Comparative Analysis of U.S.-Japan Copyright Law and Responsibility Allocation for Infrastructure Providers and Users
abstract: Abstract:This research monograph provides a rigorous comparative legal and corporate governance analysis of data procurement in frontier generative artificial intelligence development. Focusing on the normative divergence between Article 30-4 of the Japanese Copyright Act and the Fair Use doctrine under 17 U.S.C. §107, we examine cross-border conflicts of law arising when data extraction, compute training, and model serving occur in separate jurisdictions. Furthermore, the paper analyzes the liability allocation between AI developers and compute/cloud infrastructure providers, distinguishing passive IaaS/PaaS conduits from integrated strategic partnerships. Grounded in Delaware corporate governance standards (the Caremark doctrine) and ESG supply-chain due diligence, we establish a practical compliance and contractual risk-allocation architecture to ensure sustainable, transparent knowledge ecosystems.
